lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
At dawn, I stood by the lake.
The water lay still.
A gentle mist drifted on the surface.
The world breathed quietly.
The light gradually appeared in the distant sky.
The sun emerged.
Its rays spread across the pure air.

[Verse 2]
No one spoke.
I gazed at the shore.
A narrow stream flowed near my feet.
The water whispered softly.
Birds sang in distant trees.
A fish jumped, and gentle ripples ran outward from the edge.

[Bridge]
From the depths of the forest, a faint presence moved.
I noticed a deer.
It stood still.
Then it vanished into the trees.
I simply observed the landscape in silence.
Nothing spoke, yet everything lived.
The morning continued.

[Outro]
A new day arose.
I remained there.
Time passed.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The library had a quiet atmosphere that afternoon.
I picked up a small essay collection and opened the first chapter.
The author gently described small discoveries in daily life.

[Verse 2]
In one paragraph he expressed a memory; in another he openly described the desires of his youth.
The writing strongly appealed to me and held my attention.
The style was as calm as a philosophy book, yet something in it inspired me.

[Bridge]
I glanced out of the window, then returned to the page.
The mind that had composed these sentences was quiet, but it was full of passion.
Outside, a small child ran past.
I watched him with curiosity.
Then I continued reading.

[Outro]
Words carry us beyond time.
Today, I preferred this one book to everything else.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
My father gave me a small box.
Inside were old photographs and one letter.
He had kept them safe for a long time.
In one photo, my young father smiled next to my grandfather.

[Verse 2]
This is my childhood, he whispered softly.
I came to see the ordinary box as something precious.
I had never imagined that a piece of paper could carry such worth.

[Bridge]
Father taught me about the bonds and affection within a family, not with words, but quietly.
The photograph gave me comfort.
He said, I give you this, and the small gift carried years of respect and memory.

[Outro]
I nodded to my father and accepted the box.
A gentle desire to give something back grew in my heart.

My father brought home a small puppy.

Mother found her gentle.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
It was an autumn afternoon.
I sat on the porch.
The breeze felt pleasant, and I observed the trees in the garden swaying slowly.
Grandmother made tea and had me hold the cup.
She always lets me read any book I like.

[Verse 2]
Today she let me rest as long as I wanted.
I could see petals drift on the wind.
I could hear a distant bird sing beyond the hedge.
Close your eyes and allow the wind to carry you, grandmother said gently.

[Bridge]
Grandfather used to admire the plum tree in our garden.
Grandmother often recalled that memory and smiles quietly.
I sensed that she wanted to encourage me to remember him.
Soon the evening sun painted the roof in gentle tones.
The garden became calm and golden.

[Outro]
Grandmother handed me a fresh cup.
I wished she would let me stay on the porch forever.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
On Monday morning, I get up at half past six.
This is my habit.
In the kitchen I make coffee and open the newspaper.
That is my daily rhythm.
At the station I take the train and commute to my office.
The journey is ordinary.

[Verse 2]
In a crowded car, many passengers stand silently.
I work for a small local company.
My coworkers are kind, and a colleague often laughs loudly.
Each person carries out their duties.
At noon we gather for lunch together.
In the afternoon, I finish one task after another.

[Bridge]
The phone rings, and a new request appears.
Work proceeds in a steady way.
In the evening the same common faces return to the station, and people rush home.
Through the train window I look beyond the tall buildings at the fading sky.

[Outro]
Within these quiet days, a small sense of purpose lives, and I believe in it.

[Verse 1]
In the evening the family gathered at the dinner table.
Mother was finishing the meal preparations.
Father said, I am going to have a drink tonight.
He had already made up his mind.
Sister wanted to discuss the trip.
She proposed that I go with her.

[Verse 2]
My brother offered, I will drive you both to the airport next weekend.
Mother mentioned a new recipe.
Father admitted, If you make pasta, I will help.
He is good at cooking.
What shall we do about dinner tomorrow?
sister asked.

Sister gave him a small nod and confirmed the plan.

[Outro]
Dinner flowed slowly, more slowly than usual.

I was discussing the Sunday picnic with my sister.
If the weather is good, we will spend the day in a meadow by the river.
If it rains, we will watch a movie at home.

[Verse 2]
Unless it rains, we will leave the house at ten in the morning.
We thought about several conditions and made a clear plan.
Tomorrow morning, unless the forecast turns much worse, we will go as planned.

[Bridge]
If it does rain, however, we will shift the picnic to the afternoon.
Whenever the forecast improves, our spirits rise with it.
Mother was tired, but she said she would prepare sandwiches.

[Outro]
As Sunday approaches, my sister's face remains calm.
The fact that everything would depend on the weather brought our family quietly together.

This time tomorrow, I will be sitting in a meeting room.
At ten I will be attending a lecture, and in the afternoon I will be finishing the new project file.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
My sister always chooses her words.
She pauses quietly first, and then she speaks.
Whenever she speaks, I recognize something deeply true in her voice.
Do not rush.
Being honest with your own emotions is the most important thing.

[Verse 2]
Her advice is always gentle, but it moves my heart.
When she listens, she shows patience.
When I share an opinion, she takes time to consider it.
Her opinion is always sincere and genuine.

[Bridge]
I hope I will one day have the calm and mature nature she has.
She encourages me, and she truly does concern herself with my future.
One evening she quietly remarked, A person can care for others only after they understand themselves.

[Outro]
Her quiet but steady words stayed with me.
Affection filled my chest gently.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
For three years I have been practicing the piano every morning.
My daily effort has slowly been paying off.
I have been working on a single piece of music for a long time.
Every day, I have continued to practice.
Sometimes I have struggled, but I have never stopped.

[Verse 2]
I used to be unable to play fast.
In the past my fingers would tangle and the notes would break.
Lately, however, my fingers have been moving in a steady way.
I have become devoted to shaping every sound.

[Bridge]
My playing has gradually been improving, and my ability has been developing.
For several months now, I have noticed slow but steady growth in myself.
Today, I accomplished something important.
At a small recital, I played all the way to the last note without stopping.

[Outro]
That small achievement was the quiet result of all the time I had spent practicing.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
When I arrived at the station, my friend had already departed on his train.
I caught my breath and sat down on the bench, feeling exhausted.
Actually, I had left home late.
The road had been under repair for some time, and I had not known the detour.

[Verse 2]
Meanwhile my friend had reached the station on time.
The staff said he had boarded the train only a few minutes before.
I had not been able to spot his face in the crowd.
I felt sorry, but there was nothing I could do.

[Bridge]
I had to wait for the next train.
Then my phone rang.
He would get off at the next station and come back for me.
I realize now that he has always shown this gentle kindness.
On a small bench in front of the station, I sat waiting for him.

[Outro]
My feelings eventually settled.
The clouds vanished, and eventually the sky grew bright.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
On the last evening of the year, I stopped by a small temple.
I had visited it at the same time last year.
This is my moment of reflection.

[Verse 2]
Looking back on the year, I think I ought to have been kinder to others.
I ought not to have said some of the words I said.
The younger me used to be short-tempered.

[Verse 3]
I used to snap at my sister almost every day.
Whenever I recall that, I feel ashamed.
But my sister would always respond with quiet patience.
In the new year, I want to be more modest.

[Bridge]
I want to express more gratitude to my family.
I want to adopt a small habit: to rise a little earlier and breathe deeply.
The temple bell rang.
I pressed my hands together and quietly recalled my late grandfather.

[Outro]
He used to say, A person does not need to speak many words.
I want to inherit that quiet advice now.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
That day I hesitated in front of a small shop.
Should I buy the red gloves, or not?
It was a moment of quick decision.
Now I think I should have bought them.

[Verse 2]
I ought to have made my decision earlier, in time for my sister's birthday.
The next day I returned, but the gloves were already gone.
The shopkeeper said, Yesterday another customer had bought them.

[Bridge]
I did not confess my regret to my sister.
She seemed not to mind and simply smiled at me kindly.
Perhaps I should have been more honest.
But she had already forgiven me.

[Outro]
In that small moment, her maturity became clear.
A person may regret, yet be saved by another person's affection.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In my town, an old Western style house has remained.
It had long been forgotten, but one year the townspeople decided that it would be restored.
The house had been constructed about eighty years ago.
After the war it was abandoned for a long time.

[Verse 2]
Its roof had crumbled, and the garden was covered with weeds.
Citizens raised their voices, saying this building should be preserved as part of our heritage.
The house was recognized as historically significant.

[Bridge]

On the day it opened, I stepped inside.
In its old pillars, traces of the past were carved.

[Outro]
Through the efforts of local people, the old building was given a new life.

My sister has been training for the marathon every day.
In two more weeks she will run the race.
At first, she was too exhausted to run ten kilometers and would end up walking halfway.
Her body could not yet keep up with her goal.

[Verse 2]

Lately she has enough strength to finish the full ten kilometers.

I am sure that on the race day, she will cross the finish line with a smile.

[Outro]

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Deep in the drawer of my father's desk, I discovered an old diary.
He seems to have been writing for a long time.
I hesitated to open it.
For a moment I held my breath.

[Verse 2]
Reading it would mean entering the private world of my father's heart.
But I could not avoid the temptation.
I picked it up and began reading each line.
In his youth, my father had been composing poetry.

[Bridge]
In every word, there was a joy in life, but also a small regret at the bottom of his chest.
My father is always quiet and says little.
But inside that diary, another father existed.

[Outro]
I quietly returned the diary and closed the drawer.
Glimpsing my father's past filled me with a new respect for him.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
On the morning when we reached the airport, my friend was waiting to leave for a new job abroad.
I watched him quietly.
Loading his luggage on the cart, he turned toward me.
Though smiling, his eyes seemed a little wet.

[Verse 2]
We gave each other a brief hug and exchanged a small promise.
Walking toward the gate, he did not turn back.
Wishing him well in my heart, I saw him off.
Not turning back was probably the better way, I thought.

[Bridge]
My friend, having shared many years with me, was leaving to follow a new path.
We had promised to keep in touch.
Through the large glass window of the airport, I watched his plane depart.
In the morning light, the plane slowly rose into the sky.

[Outro]
The future awaiting my friend seemed to spread beyond the clouds.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
I visited the home of the teacher who had guided me during my university years.
It had been ten years.
He was the person whom students of my generation had respected most.

[Verse 2]
He lived in an old house which had a quiet garden.
The figure who appeared at the door looked much older than before, yet his eyes were the same as long ago.

[Verse 3]
In his study, thousands of books stood on the shelves.
Among them were some manuscripts that he himself had written.
He recommended one book to me, saying, This is the book which I wanted you to read when you were young.

[Bridge]
The book that I had wanted to read turned out to be exactly this one.
He served me tea with the same gentleness that he had shown when I was his student.

[Outro]
What I discovered was a bundle of letters from scholars with whom he had been corresponding for many years.
Those letters were the source of his wisdom.

[Verse 1]
Lately, I have been thinking about what is important to me.
What matters most seems to be the essentials.
What I had pursued for a long time was not always significant.

[Verse 2]
What truly matters is the small meal with family, the call from a friend, the single book before sleep.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
My grandfather worked for many years as the keeper of a lighthouse in a seaside town.
That town was the place where he lived his whole life.
Every night he would climb the stairs of the tower.

[Verse 2]
He checked the lamp, wiped the windows, and when a storm approached, he worked through the whole night without sleep.
Every summer I visited his house and looked up at the light.
The moment when the lighthouse began to glow was the time when I most wished to be there.

[Bridge]
Once he revealed to me the reason why he had continued this work.
So that ships that come back from across the sea can enter the harbor safely, he said.
I often think of the way he guided sailors.

[Outro]
Between my grandfather and the lighthouse was a long bond that needed no words.
I could never imagine how many sailors his light had guided on stormy nights.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
A small concert was held in the town hall.
Whoever came could enter with free admission.
Whoever performed was warmly welcomed by the audience.
The first to perform was a girl of ten, holding a violin.

[Verse 2]
When she finished, however softly she played, every note reached the listeners in the room.
Applause rose several times.
Whichever movement she played, her tone was pure.

[Bridge]
Whoever listened could not help but admire the purity of her sound.
That evening, the hall was more peaceful than I had ever seen, and people exchanged smile after smile with one another.

[Outro]
This kind of place, whenever it exists, is a small community tradition that I want to treasure.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
If I were a bird, I would fly freely wherever I wished.
In the morning I would pass through the forest, at noon I would cross the valley, and at night I would sleep beside the stars.

[Verse 2]
If I had wings, I would soar above the clouds.
I would not feel constrained by the distance to faraway cities.
If I were not bound to the ground, I would surely travel wherever the wind carried me.
Yet, now I stand on the Earth.

[Bridge]
I am not a bird.
I can only imagine.
Still, to imagine is a small form of freedom.
Looking up at the evening sky, I think: if I were a bird, how deeply would I admire this sky?

[Outro]
Standing on the ground, I still look up at the same sky.
Imagination embraces me instead.

[Verse 1]
If I had sent the letter that day, everything might have been different.
My childhood friend had moved to a distant town.
All I had to do was write a single word of thanks.
A single letter would have been enough.

[Verse 2]
If I had had a little more courage at the time, the letter would have reached her, and she might have remembered me for longer.
But I did not put it into words.
I hid my words away, treasuring them too carefully.

[Bridge]

If I had written that one letter, I might have been corresponding with her to this day.
Long after, when I heard the news of her marriage, I tasted that small regret once more.

[Outro]
I learned that a life can turn on the courage it takes to send a single letter.

If I had had a little more courage at the time, the letter would have reached her, and she might have remembered me for longer.

If I had written that one letter, I might have been corresponding with her to this day.
Long after, when I heard the news of her marriage, I tasted that small regret once more.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The discovery of penicillin began with an accident.
In 1928, in a laboratory in London, a scientist returned from his vacation.
Alexander Fleming noticed that a strange mold had grown on one of the dishes left on his bench.

[Verse 2]
Around the mold, the bacteria had vanished.
How much the world would have lost if Fleming had missed that small observation!

[Bridge]
If he had not noticed that mold, many infections might not have been treated, and countless lives might have been lost because of wounds on the battlefield.
That one dish helped open the age of antibiotics.

[Outro]
Fleming's careful observation, followed by the work of many other scientists, eventually helped save millions of lives.
If that chance observation had never been made, the history of science would have been utterly different.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
What is the oldest tree in the world?
Many people think of a great oak.
But there is an ancient tree far older than any oak.

[Verse 2]
High in the mountains of California, a bristlecone pine has survived for over four thousand years.
It is one of the oldest living trees on Earth.
The bristlecone pine grows slowly.

[Verse 3]
Compared with other pines, it may add only a few millimeters each year.
But it is far stronger.
In the high mountains, the air is thin, the wind is cold, and the soil is poor.

[Bridge]
Yet such a harsh environment is what has enabled the long life of this tree.
Scientists measure the age of these trees from growth rings within the wood.

[Outro]
One has been found to be more than four thousand eight hundred years old.
We cannot help admiring a tree that is older than many civilizations.
It is among the most remarkable living beings, carrying silence and strength together.

[Verse 1]
Marie Curie was born in Poland and later moved to Paris.
Her name, Marie Curie, is one of the most famous physicists in the history of science.
Her passion, namely her devotion to science, was extraordinary.

[Verse 2]
Together with her husband Pierre, she devoted much of her life to research.
Their goal, to isolate and study the new element radium, meant years of endless difficulty.

The couple continued despite the risk, exposing themselves to radiation.

Her achievement of winning two Nobel Prizes could not have come without her pure love of study, namely her passion.
As a woman, a mother, and a scientist, she opened a path for later generations.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In December 1955, on a bus in Montgomery, Alabama, a Black woman named Rosa Parks was ordered to give her seat to a white passenger.
No.
How short, how quiet those words were!
Yet her single word changed the course of American history.
She was arrested on the spot.

[Verse 2]
In those days, the law separated the races, and Black people could only sit in certain seats.
The law, which had made discrimination a system, had long cast a shadow on society.
Parks' refusal sparked the Montgomery Bus Boycott.

[Bridge]
Reverend Martin Luther King led the way, and the Black citizens of the town stopped riding the buses.
What a strong protest it was!
The following year, a federal court ruled bus segregation unconstitutional, and the U.S. Supreme Court upheld that decision.

[Outro]
The No of a single citizen helped change society.
Let us never forget such a single word, filled with courage.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Isaac Newton, in his later years, described himself as someone who still knew very little compared with the vast unknown.
Few people have ever given humanity such great knowledge.

[Verse 2]
The law of gravity, the three laws of motion, the development of calculus.
Before Newton, no single theory explained both falling objects and planetary orbits.
His mathematics itself rebuilt the very language of science.

[Bridge]
Yet he never allowed himself to become proud.
He compared himself to a child on the seashore, finding only a few interesting stones.
Before him, he said, the vast ocean of truth remained largely unexplored.

[Outro]
Newton's humility teaches us that however much one knows, it is never enough.
Theory may extend far, but the ocean of knowledge is deeper still.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Antoni Gaudí, from the end of the nineteenth century through the early twentieth, was the architect who created a unique architectural language in Barcelona, Spain.
His most famous work is the basilica known as the Sagrada Família.

[Verse 2]
For more than a hundred years, its construction has continued, with interruptions.
It is an unfinished masterpiece.
Gaudí drew inspiration for his designs in nature.
Trees, mountains, shells, bones, waves.
Every column, every curve, was designed from a form found in nature.

[Bridge]
He described nature as his great teacher.
For him, nature itself was a form of architecture.
In 1926, Gaudí was struck by a tram and died from his injuries several days later.

[Outro]
The cathedral, however, is still being built, century after century, through donations and support from visitors around the world.
Perhaps its unfinished state has itself become part of the building's history.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In 1831, Charles Darwin began a voyage around the world aboard a British survey ship.
During the five years of that expedition, he visited many islands along the coast of South America.

[Verse 2]
On the Galapagos Islands, he carefully observed how animals varied from island to island.
He collected birds that were later identified in England as related finch species with different beaks.
Darwin collected many specimens and, after his return, spent long years in thought.

[Bridge]
Why were there different animals on different islands?
Why had they adapted so perfectly to each environment?
In 1859, the publication of his book, On the Origin of Species, shook the world.
The concept of evolution shook the belief of the age.

[Outro]
Although there was fierce criticism, Darwin's theory, over time, came to be accepted.
Nature, quietly yet deeply, continues to change from generation to generation.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Twenty-four hundred years ago, in ancient Athens, there lived a philosopher named Socrates.
He never wrote a book.
His philosophy existed only in the dialogues he held with other people.
In Plato's account, Socrates said that an unexamined life was not worth living.

[Verse 2]
Socrates kept asking people what virtue was.
He asked what justice was.
He would claim that he himself did not know, and then question those who claimed to know.
His questions slowly shook the authority of those people.

[Bridge]
In 399 BC, Socrates was accused of corrupting the young and was condemned at his trial.
Friends urged him to flee, but he replied that escaping would betray the laws under which he had lived.
He drank the hemlock and died quietly.

[Outro]
But after more than two thousand years, his question still challenges us: do we examine our own lives?

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Ludwig van Beethoven, starting in his late twenties, slowly began to lose his hearing.
For a musician, no suffering could have been greater.
Yet silence did not stop the music inside him.

[Verse 2]
Deafness drove him toward despair, yet he continued to compose music of extraordinary depth.
In 1824, his final completed symphony, the Ninth, received its first performance.

[Verse 3]
It was a grand composition, using a choir to sing Schiller's poem, Ode to Joy.
On the night of the first performance, Beethoven stood on the stage.
He faced the podium, but he could no longer hear any sound.

[Bridge]
After the final note, applause filled the hall, yet he stood with his back turned, not noticing.
One of the soloists gently touched his arm and made him turn around.
Before him, the audience was on its feet, applauding.

[Outro]
Silence did not lock him inside.
Through silence, he continued to reach toward humanity.
The Ninth is a testament to the creativity Beethoven sustained through profound suffering.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
On December 17, 1903, on a sand dune at Kitty Hawk, North Carolina, the Wright brothers succeeded in a twelve-second flight.
They were brothers who, while running a bicycle shop, had kept pursuing a dream of flying.

[Verse 2]
Wilbur and Orville, with their own hands, built a wind tunnel and examined the shape of wings over and over again.
Many people said it was impossible.
But the brothers never abandoned their dream.

[Verse 3]
If birds can fly, we surely can too, they believed.
The wind was strong that morning.
The aircraft, carrying Orville, made its brief flight of twelve seconds.
The distance was about thirty-seven meters.

[Bridge]
Yet that moment was the result of a long effort to achieve controlled, powered flight.
When Orville landed, the brothers knew that years of work had finally taken flight.

[Outro]
To be called an inventor meant nothing to them at that instant.
It was the very first step that humanity had taken toward the sky.

[Verse 1]
We look up at the night sky.
At that moment, what we see is light that has traveled for thousands of years.
In 1609, Galileo Galilei looked at the sky through a telescope he had built himself.

[Verse 2]
There were mountains on the face of the moon.
Around Jupiter, there were four moons.
These observations shook the ancient belief that the Earth stood at the center of the universe.
The church condemned him.
But truth was not erased.

[Verse 3]
Four hundred years later, in 1977, NASA launched two probes.
Voyager 1 and 2.
They explored Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, and Neptune in turn.
Even now, they continue their quiet journey beyond the solar system.
Each Voyager probe carries a Golden Record.

[Bridge]
The sounds of Earth, human words, human music.
It is a small message from humanity to any being who might, someday, find it somewhere in the vast universe.

[Outro]
From Galileo's telescope to Voyager's journey, our curiosity continues across the centuries, toward the far end of the universe.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In 1953, James Watson and Francis Crick published their discovery that DNA has the structure of a double helix.
But there was another scientist whose contribution was essential: Rosalind Franklin.
In her laboratory at King's College London, she was producing images of DNA using X-ray diffraction.

[Verse 2]
One photograph, known as Photo 51, revealed an X-shaped pattern that provided crucial evidence for a helical structure.
But her photograph was shown to Watson without her knowledge.
The Nobel Prize was given in 1962 to Watson, Crick, and Wilkins.

[Bridge]
By then, Franklin was no longer in this world.
She had died in 1958, at only thirty-seven.
Under Nobel rules, the prize is not normally awarded posthumously.
Rosalind Franklin's dedication was underestimated for a long time.
Now, we must remember her quiet contribution.

[Outro]
The history of science is not made by loud voices alone.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
During the Second World War, at Bletchley Park in Britain, the young mathematician Alan Turing was trying to crack the German Enigma cipher.
Every day, the German submarine fleet exchanged encrypted messages.
If they could not be decoded, Allied ships could be sunk one after another.

[Verse 2]
Turing, with his colleagues, built a machine called the Bombe.
The machine rapidly eliminated impossible Enigma settings, helping the team read many messages.
After the war, Turing explored the question, Can a machine think?

[Bridge]
His work became foundational to computer science and later debates about artificial intelligence.
But under the law of his time, homosexuality was criminalized, and he was prosecuted.
He died at forty-one.
The country he had helped defend later punished him for who he was.

[Outro]
In 2013, Queen Elizabeth II granted him an official pardon.
The pardon came far too late.

[Verse 1]
The Silk Road, from ancient times, connected Asia in the east and Europe in the west.
It was not a single road, but a network of many routes.
Chinese silk, Persian glass, Indian spices, and Roman gold traveled this road by caravan.

[Verse 2]
Merchants loaded their camels and crossed deserts and mountains.
But it was not only goods that traveled this road.
Religion also spread along this path.
Buddhism spread from India to China; Islam spread from Arabia into Central Asia.
Language and art were also exchanged.

[Bridge]
The Chinese way of making paper traveled westward and later contributed to learning and culture in Europe.
The Silk Road was one of history's great networks of exchange.

[Outro]
The words carried by the desert wind, across many centuries, still quietly support the roots of many civilizations.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In 1962, the American marine biologist Rachel Carson published a book called Silent Spring.
It was a book that warned how much the use of chemical pesticides were destroying nature.
At the time, DDT was being used in great amounts to kill insects.

[Verse 2]
But pesticides did not kill only insects.
Birds, fish, and human beings as well were being harmed by the poison that accumulated in their bodies over time.
Carson warned that spring might come with no birds singing.
Carson's words awakened widespread public concern.

[Bridge]
The chemical industry attacked her violently and criticized her work.
But her warning was eventually accepted, and the United States banned most uses of DDT.
Carson's book helped inspire the growth of the modern environmental movement.

[Outro]
To preserve the ecological balance is also to preserve humanity itself.

On March 12, 1930, the Indian leader Mohandas Gandhi, with seventy-eight companions, began to walk toward the coast of Dandi.
The distance was about three hundred eighty-five kilometers.
The journey would last twenty-four days.

[Verse 2]
Along the way, more and more people joined, and the march grew to thousands.
What was the purpose?
To make salt at the seashore.

[Verse 3]
At the time, the British colonial rule maintained a salt monopoly and prohibited Indians from producing or selling salt independently.
The salt tax weighed most heavily on the poorest.

[Bridge]
The moment Gandhi picked up a handful of salt from the sand, British rule was quietly, yet deeply shaken.
This was a disciplined, nonviolent protest, carrying no weapons.
Gandhi was imprisoned many times by the British.

[Verse 4]
But his nonviolent movement contributed to the movement for Indian independence and inspired movements throughout the world.
Martin Luther King Jr. later drew deeply from Gandhi's philosophy of nonviolent resistance.

[Outro]
Movements around the world adapted its lessons in their own struggles for justice.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In the desert at Giza, in Egypt, three pyramids stand.
The largest, the pyramid of Khufu, has been standing there for four thousand five hundred years.
Its height is one hundred forty-six meters.

[Verse 2]
It was constructed of about two point three million stone blocks.
At the time, no such enormous building existed anywhere in the world.
How the ancient Egyptians built it is still not fully known.

[Verse 3]
Leading explanations involve ramps and organized teams transporting heavy limestone blocks, though the exact methods remain debated.
The pyramid was built as the pharaoh's tomb and part of a larger burial complex.

[Bridge]
The Egyptians believed in life after death, and its form and burial complex reflected their beliefs about kingship and the afterlife.
The silence of four thousand five hundred years still rests quietly in the wind.

[Outro]
The ancient kingdom ended long ago, but its silence still seems to speak to us.
The wish of the people who sought immortality has been carved into stone, and it still survives today.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The principle of democracy rests on the idea that people govern themselves.
In ancient Athens, citizens gathered in the public square and discussed policy.
This was the starting point of the democracy that would later spread throughout the world.

[Verse 2]
Modern democratic states almost always have a supreme law called a constitution.
The constitution limits the power of government and protects the rights of the citizens.
In many countries, citizens choose their representatives through elections held every few years.

[Verse 3]
Candidates run campaigns and present their policies to the voters.
The elected representatives gather in parliament or in congress, where they create new legislation.
After discussion in committee, a bill becomes law.
The duty of a citizen is not only to vote.

[Bridge]
It is also to take an interest in social problems and to participate in politics throughout life.
How to balance the will of the majority with the freedom of the minority is the challenge of every democratic state.

[Outro]
To respect the will of the majority while protecting the freedom of the minority — this is the essential responsibility of a democratic society.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In a market economy, the price of most goods and services is determined by demand and supply.
When consumers strongly demand a certain product, prices rise.
When demand falls, prices fall as well.
This is the most basic mechanism of the market.

[Verse 2]
A company gathers capital, conducts production in a factory, and sells its products to earn a profit.
In an industry where competition is strong, companies are pushed to improve their quality.
Workers provide labor and, in return, receive wages or salaries.

[Bridge]
When employment is stable, the income of households is also stable.
A nation raises funds through taxes and uses them to fund education and welfare.
A bank provides loans, and companies grow through investment.

[Outro]
In the modern era, where globalization has advanced, the economy of one country is closely tied to the markets of others.
Exports and imports support growth.
Economies, beyond the borders of states, continually influence one another.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
A modern corporation spends a great deal on advertising in order to make its brand known to as many people as possible.
Through media such as television, newspapers, magazines, and the internet, countless advertisements reach us every day.

[Verse 2]
The purpose of an advertisement is to attract the attention of the consumer and persuade consumers to make a purchase.
The image of a brand, just as much as the quality of a product, has influence over our choice.

[Verse 3]
Since the appearance of social media, consumers themselves have been able to broadcast their opinions to the world.
An opinion against a certain brand can spread across the internet within hours, and the image of a corporation may shift overnight.

[Bridge]
Governments, too, have established regulations to protect consumers from misleading advertising.
For example, products related to health may not make any claim without solid evidence.

[Outro]
Today's consumption society binds corporations, consumers, and the state in a triangular relationship in which each watches the others.
We ourselves are required to keep a critical eye on what we are shown.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The climate of our planet has been changing rapidly since the industrial revolution.
The global average temperature has already risen by about 1.1 degrees.
One of the main causes is the emission of carbon dioxide produced by the burning of fossil fuels.

[Verse 2]
Deforestation and agricultural practices are also deeply involved.
As a result, sea levels rise, floods and droughts have become more frequent, and typhoons have grown stronger than ever before.
Ecosystems are being destroyed, and many species are facing the threat of extinction.

[Verse 3]
In 1997, the Kyoto Protocol was adopted, and each country was given a target for the reduction of greenhouse gases.
In 2015, the Paris Agreement was reached, and the world set its goal of keeping the rise in temperature within 1.5 degrees.

[Bridge]
Each country has begun to increase investment in renewable energy and to regulate emissions from cars and factories.
But climate change is no longer a problem that one country can solve by itself.
Without international cooperation, we cannot protect the future of the Earth.

[Outro]
The achievement of a sustainable society is now a shared goal across generations.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Education is a basic right of every person.
The United Nations has declared the right to education as one of the universal human rights.

[Verse 2]
In reality, however, the opportunity for education differs greatly depending on the country where one is born and one's family income.
There are still tens of millions of children worldwide who cannot attend school.

[Verse 3]
Even among developed countries, there are large gaps in access to and the quality of education.
The economic condition of a family greatly shapes a child's future career.
Education is not only the passing on of knowledge.

[Bridge]
It is a process by which an individual forms their identity and grows into a responsible member of society.
Many countries, through scholarships and reduced tuition, are trying to open the opportunity for higher education to more young people.

[Outro]
The reform proceeds slowly, but it does proceed.
To create a truly equal society, every child must be given the same opportunity for education.
Only when education is equal does the gap in society begin to close.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Artificial intelligence, that is, AI, has made remarkable progress over the past ten years.
Algorithms that learn from vast amounts of data now support humans in many fields, including medicine, finance, and transportation.
Diagnostic assistance, self-driving cars, and natural language processing.

[Verse 2]
Each application is changing our lives.
In some industries, automation has already transformed the landscape of labor.
But rapid technological progress comes with serious risks as well.
Invasion of privacy, the loss of jobs, the spread of misinformation.

[Verse 3]
Our society must face these consequences head on.
Who bears the responsibility for an algorithm?
When a self-driving car causes an accident, who is held accountable in court?
These questions still do not have complete answers.

[Bridge]
Governments around the world have begun to develop regulations for AI.
The European Union has already established a comprehensive law concerning the ethical use of AI.
Technology in itself is neutral.

[Outro]
Whether it is used for an ethical purpose or not depends on our human judgment.
AI must exist not so that it can think in our place, but so that we can think better than before.

lessons.style: Hopeful ambient pop, 88 BPM, clear piano motif, warm pads, acoustic-electronic percussion, and soft strings. Respectful and resilient, never sensational or melodramatic. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
At the end of 2019, in Wuhan, China, a new virus was discovered.
Within a few weeks, it had spread across borders to the rest of the world.
In March 2020, the World Health Organization declared it a pandemic.

[Verse 2]
Countries imposed lockdowns, and schools and many businesses were closed.
Infected patients were taken to hospitals across each region.
Intensive care units quickly filled up.
Doctors and nurses worked without regard to their own risk.

[Verse 3]
Symptoms differed from one person to another.
Fever, cough, and shortness of breath were common.
Most cases were mild, but elderly people and those with existing diseases became seriously ill more easily.
Researchers developed a vaccine at an unprecedented speed.

[Bridge]
Within just over a year, several vaccines were approved, and vaccination began throughout the world.
The pandemic has left us many lessons.
How vital public health preparedness is.
How without international cooperation, infectious diseases cannot be stopped.

[Outro]
To prepare for the next crisis, we must not forget these lessons.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
At the start of the twentieth century, only about one in ten of the world's population lived in an urban area.
Today, more than half live in cities.

[Verse 2]
Urbanization has concentrated opportunities for jobs, education, and medical care, but it has also brought serious problems.
Traffic congestion, the high price of housing, and air pollution are among them.
Tokyo, New York, London, Shanghai.

[Verse 3]
Each of these major cities of the world faces the limits of population density and infrastructure.
In recent years, each city has begun to attempt a more sustainable form of urban planning.

[Bridge]
They are creating more roads for pedestrians and cyclists, restoring green parks, and increasing investment in public transportation.
At the same time, people have started to move from city centers to the suburbs.

[Outro]
With the spread of remote work, the distinction between urban and rural life has become less rigid.
Cities will continue to change their shape.
What matters is how we design a space in which everyone can live with peace of mind.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The ancient Olympics in Greece were a festival of peace, even halting wars during the games.
The modern Olympics inherit that spirit.
Athletes from across the world, after long years of training, step into competition.

[Verse 2]
Their discipline and dedication are more precious than anything else.
Victory is not everything.
Sportsmanship, the spirit of respecting an opponent and following the rules, is the true meaning of sport.

[Verse 3]
In recent years, the doping problem has shaken competition around the world.
Athletes who use banned drugs lose their medals and are removed from their sport.
To preserve the principle of fair play, strict testing is essential.

[Bridge]
Winning teams gather enthusiastic fans, and losing teams receive quiet applause.
To accept defeat and turn toward the next challenge — this is the true beauty of sport.
Children in front of the television look up to these athletes.

[Outro]
As role models, they pass on to a younger generation the message that effort can bear fruit.

Dignified documentary mood that gradually opens toward hope. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Japan is one of the most rapidly aging societies in the world.
The population aged 65 and above already makes up over 28 percent of the whole.
A long life is something to be celebrated, yet our society faces new challenges.

[Verse 2]
The workforce is declining, and the pension system has become harder to sustain.
Medical costs for older people increase each year, putting pressure on the national budget.
How to sustain welfare is a common challenge for every developed country.

[Verse 3]
The form of the family has also changed.
More elderly now live apart from their children and grandchildren, and a new problem has appeared: loneliness.
Local communities have begun various efforts to support elderly people who live alone.

[Bridge]
Volunteers visit them regularly, and care facilities are trying to make up for the shortage of staff with new technology.
The mutual support between generations will be the foundation of our future society.

[Outro]
The young and the old, each respecting and supporting the other.
This is what creates the true richness of a long-lived society.

lessons.style: Thoughtful cinematic indie pop, 88 BPM, steady 4/4, warm piano, brushed drums, subtle bass pulse, and restrained low strings. Dignified documentary mood that gradually opens toward hope. Add a quiet newsroom pulse and a serious, watchful atmosphere. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In a democratic society, the press has been called the fourth estate.
Alongside the legislative, the executive, and the judicial, it is one of the pillars that supports society.

[Verse 2]
Journalists carry the role of revealing wrongdoing in government and business and passing that on to the citizens.
Investigative reporting has often been the trigger that has changed society.

[Verse 3]
In 1972, during the Watergate scandal, two young reporters helped expose abuses of power that led to the American president's resignation.
That was an example of how the press can hold even the highest authorities accountable.

[Bridge]
In our time, however, the reliability of information has become a great challenge.
Information sent out without checking the source, deliberate disinformation.
These can twist the judgment of society.

[Verse 4]
Under dictatorships in various countries, censorship is common, and it is not rare for journalists to be imprisoned.
Press freedom is not taken for granted in every country.
As receivers of information, we must develop the ability to judge what is a reliable source.

[Outro]
To protect the freedom of the press is, in the end, to protect our own freedom.

lessons.style: Atmospheric cinematic synth-pop, 84 BPM, glassy pads, soft mallets, delicate arpeggiators, piano, and slowly widening strings. A sense of discovery, scale, and quiet wonder. Add faint electrical-coil textures and an early-industrial sense of wonder around Tesla's dream. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Nikola Tesla was born in 1856 in Smiljan, in what is now Croatia.
He later moved to America and, from the late nineteenth to the early twentieth century, became an immigrant inventor who transformed the world of electricity.

[Verse 2]
His greatest contribution was to make alternating current electricity practical.
At the time, Thomas Edison was promoting direct current.
Tesla argued for the advantage of alternating current for long-distance transmission, and a war of currents arose between them.

[Verse 3]
As a result, the alternating current system became the standard of the world's power grid.
Today, almost all of the electricity that reaches our homes owes much to the vision that Tesla pursued.
Tesla's imagination did not stop there.

[Bridge]
He had already envisioned the foundations of wireless communication, wireless power transmission, radio, and radar in Edison's age.
However, his life was never happy.
His business partnership did not go well, and his Wardenclyffe Tower project collapsed for lack of funding.

[Verse 4]
Many of his patents did not bring him enough reward.
Tesla died in 1943, in a hotel room in New York, in poverty.
The recognition of his genius spread widely only after his death.

[Outro]
Today, we drive cars that bear his name and live within part of the future that he had imagined.

lessons.title: H058 — 司法と裁判
lessons.style: Thoughtful cinematic indie pop, 88 BPM, steady 4/4, warm piano, brushed drums, subtle bass pulse, and restrained low strings. Dignified documentary mood that gradually opens toward hope. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The court system of modern society is a way to settle conflict through law, not through violence.
When an incident occurs, the police first begin an investigation and arrest a suspect.
Then the prosecution gathers evidence and decides whether to bring charges.

[Verse 2]
When the trial begins, the prosecution and the defense each present their arguments.
Witnesses are called to the court and, after taking an oath, give their testimony.
The defendant also has the right to defend himself with the help of an attorney.

[Verse 3]
In many countries, a trial is presided over by a judge.
In serious criminal cases, some countries use a jury of citizens to decide the facts.
Innocent until proven guilty.
A person is presumed innocent until guilt is proven.
This is one of the most important principles of modern law.

[Bridge]
If the evidence is not sufficient, the defendant is found not guilty.
If the verdict is guilty, a sentence is given.
The punishment may be prison time, a fine, or community service.
If the defendant disagrees with the judgment, he can appeal to a higher court.

[Outro]
The system of justice must be fair to both victims and offenders.
To realize the ideal of justice, humanity has spent centuries refining the system of the court.

lessons.title: H059 — 心理学と意思決定
lessons.style: Spacious chamber-pop, 78 BPM, felt piano, cello, subtle ambient texture, and minimal percussion. Reflective, intimate, and intellectually calm, leaving breathing room between ideas. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Psychology is the discipline that studies human behavior and the workings of the mind in a scientific way.
At the end of the nineteenth century, Wilhelm Wundt founded the world's first psychology laboratory at the University of Leipzig.

[Verse 2]
That moment is regarded as the academic beginning of the field.
In the early twentieth century, the Russian Ivan Pavlov observed that a dog produced saliva when it saw food.

[Verse 3]
He further discovered that, when a bell was rung repeatedly before the food, the dog began to produce saliva at the sound of the bell alone.
This is the phenomenon known as classical conditioning.

[Bridge]
Sigmund Freud argued that our unconscious desires were what drove much of our behavior.
His theory caused much debate, but his great contribution was to spread the concept of the unconscious into the world.

[Verse 4]
In the 1960s, Stanley Milgram's experiments showed how ordinary people, under the instruction of an authority figure, could perform cruel actions.
This became one of the most shocking findings of social psychology.
Recent research has revealed how often our decisions are distorted by many biases.

[Outro]
Though we wish to be rational, we are easily turned aside by emotion and assumption.
Therapy for people experiencing anxiety or depression has also been a great contribution of psychology.
The science of the mind is a tool by which we may better understand ourselves.

In the 1960s, Stanley Milgram's experiments showed how ordinary people, under the instruction of an authority figure, could perform cruel actions.
This became one of the most shocking findings of social psychology.
Recent research has revealed how often our decisions are distorted by many biases.
Though we wish to be rational, we are easily turned aside by emotion and assumption.
Therapy for people experiencing anxiety or depression has also been a great contribution of psychology.
The science of the mind is a tool by which we may better understand ourselves.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
On August 6, 1945, the world's first atomic bomb was dropped on Hiroshima.
Three days later, a second one was dropped on Nagasaki.
In both cities, over 200,000 people lost their lives, either at once or in the months that followed.

[Verse 2]
After the war, the world entered the age of nuclear weapons.
The United States and the Soviet Union raced to develop nuclear arms, and the conflict between the two camps was called the Cold War.
The threat of conflict reached every corner of the world.

[Verse 3]
A world frightened by the danger of nuclear war signed the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty, the NPT, in 1968.
It is an international treaty that tries to prevent more countries from holding nuclear weapons.
But even after the Cold War ended, conflict in the world has not vanished.

[Bridge]
Regional wars continue, and the number of refugees keeps rising.
Syria, Ukraine, Sudan, Myanmar.
Many victims have been driven from their homes.
The United Nations has provided a place for negotiation and mediation to prevent war.

[Verse 4]
But when the permanent members of the Security Council disagree, the UN becomes powerless.
The limit of diplomacy remains a great challenge.
Peace is not simply the absence of war.

[Outro]
True peace is born only when there is the will to respect one another, to speak with one another, and to seek reconciliation.
To pass on the memory of Hiroshima and Nagasaki across generations is our responsibility for the future.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In 1856, in a small monastery of the Austrian Empire, a monk began to plant pea seeds.
His name was Gregor Mendel.
Mendel paid attention to the traits of pea plants — their height, seed color, and seed shape.

[Verse 2]
For many years, he crossbred tens of thousands of plants and recorded each result with care.
When he crossed a tall parent with a short parent, the offspring were all tall.

[Verse 3]
But when he crossed those tall offspring among themselves, short plants appeared again in the next generation.
The ratio was about three to one.
From this observation, Mendel reasoned that a trait was inherited from parent to offspring through two elements.

[Bridge]
One was a dominant element that appeared on the surface; the other was a recessive element that was hidden.
In 1865, he presented his discovery to a local scientific society.
But its importance was hardly understood by the scientists of the time.

[Verse 4]
His paper lay buried in dust for decades.
At the start of the twentieth century, three independent researchers rediscovered Mendel's laws.
His experiments finally came to be recognized as the starting point of modern genetics.

[Outro]
In a quiet monastery, a single monk who kept facing his pea plants was the first to bring the light of science to the way life is inherited.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Every year, about eight million tons of plastic flow into the world's oceans.
That equals one truckload every minute.
In the Pacific Ocean, a huge area of garbage twice the size of Texas is floating, called the Great Pacific Garbage Patch.

[Verse 2]
Debris carried by the currents has gathered there over many years.
Larger pieces of plastic, broken down by waves and ultraviolet light, slowly becomes microplastic.
These tiny particles enter the food chain, from plankton to fish, and eventually onto our dinner tables.

[Verse 3]
The impact on marine life is severe.
Whales and seabirds have mistaken plastic bags for food and have died after swallowing them.
Coral reefs, too, face the double threat of chemical pollution and warming waters.

[Bridge]
Governments around the world have introduced various policies, such as charging for plastic bags and banning certain plastics.
Companies, on the other hand, have invested in biodegradable materials and recycling technology.

[Outro]
In the end, the problem will be solved by the choices each of us makes.
Reduce, reuse, recycle.
The accumulation of small choices in daily life will change the future of the ocean.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In 1960, a twenty-six-year-old English woman named Jane Goodall walked alone into the forest of Tanzania, in East Africa.
Her aim was to observe wild chimpanzees in their own natural environment.

[Verse 2]
In those days, it was almost unprecedented for a woman to enter the interior of Africa by herself.
She did not even have a university degree.
But the paleontologist Louis Leakey believed in her passion and patience and supported her.

[Verse 3]
In the forest of Gombe, she sat for months without showing herself, deep among the trees.
After a while, the chimpanzees stopped fearing her and began to show her glimpses of their daily lives.

[Bridge]
Her greatest discovery was the observation that chimpanzees made twigs into tools for catching termites.
To the world of science, which had until then believed that only humans used tools, this came as a great shock.

[Verse 4]
Goodall also showed that chimpanzees had emotions similar to those of humans — family bonds, sadness, and conflict.
Her observations redrew, from the very ground, the line between humanity and other animals.
In her later years, Goodall devoted herself to the conservation of wildlife.

[Outro]
The youth program she founded, called Roots and Shoots, has become a starting point for young people in over sixty countries to take on environmental issues in their own neighborhoods.
Hope lies in action.
Her words remain, even now, a steady encouragement for the many young people who carry concern for the future.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Pablo Picasso was born in 1881 in Malaga, Spain.
He is one of the most influential painters of the twentieth century, leaving behind tens of thousands of works in his lifetime, including sculpture, prints, and ceramics.

[Verse 2]
In his twenties, Picasso moved to Paris and for a time produced dark-toned paintings of what is called his Blue Period.
After his Rose Period, his style would change dramatically again and again.
In 1907, Picasso unveiled Les Demoiselles d'Avignon.

[Verse 3]
The work shocked the art world with its bold method of breaking the human figure into geometric shapes.
It became the starting point of a new art movement that would later be called cubism.

[Bridge]
Cubism overturned, from its very ground, the long Western tradition of painting an object from a single perspective.
Picasso and Braque drew shapes seen from many angles at once on a single canvas.

[Verse 4]
In 1937, in the middle of the Spanish Civil War, the Nazi German air force bombed the small town of Guernica.
Angered by the suffering, Picasso completed the enormous painting Guernica in only a few weeks.

[Outro]
It became a symbol that called the cruelty of war to the attention of the world.
Picasso never settled into a single style.
It took me a long time to learn to paint like a child, he said in his later years.
Perhaps no one expanded the horizon of contemporary art as widely as he did.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In the mid-1990s, the internet began to enter ordinary homes.
In the thirty years since then, our lives, our work, and the way we connect with one another have all been transformed from the ground up.

[Verse 2]
The communication that used to be done by letter or by telephone is now carried out instantly through messaging apps and social media.
Even with a friend on the other side of the earth, we can now speak face to face in real time.

[Verse 3]
The shape of work has also changed.
Through the pandemic, remote work spread rapidly.
Leaving the company office behind, more people now work from home or from a cafe, connected to the world.
But new problems have also been created.
The question of privacy.

[Bridge]
The threats to security.
The spread of fake news and misinformation.
Who guarantees the quality of the information we receive, and how?
Social media algorithms are designed to attract our attention.

[Verse 4]
Many of us have noticed, at one moment or another, that they have been staring at their smartphone for hours.
Addiction and digital dependency have become serious problems in modern life.
The internet itself is only a useful tool.

[Outro]
What we use it for, and how we keep our distance from it, depends on the judgment of each one of us.
How to live as a human being inside the digital age — that is the challenge of the generations to come.

lessons.style: Cinematic folk-orchestral song, 82 BPM, piano, acoustic guitar, measured frame drums, cello, and gradually expanding strings. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Ancient Rome is said to have been founded in 753 BC.
For its first few centuries, it was a kingdom and then a republic centered on a small city on the Mediterranean.

[Verse 2]
By the second century BC, Rome had united the Italian peninsula and, after a long war with Carthage, taken control of the Mediterranean.
The senate and the consuls of the republic governed this vast territory.
In the first century BC, Julius Caesar appeared.

[Verse 3]
He conquered Gaul and brought to Rome vast wealth and territory.
Eventually he became dictator for life, but in 44 BC he was assassinated by senators.
His successor Octavian, in 27 BC, was given the title Augustus by the senate and became the first emperor.

[Bridge]
Through this, Rome was transformed from a republic into an empire.
The two centuries that followed are called the Pax Romana, a period of prosperity.
The whole shore of the Mediterranean fell under Roman rule, and roads were built, with aqueducts, the Colosseum, and baths constructed across the lands.

[Verse 4]
But from the third century onward, the Roman Empire would suffer from internal disorder and invasions by outside forces.
In 395, the empire split into east and west, and in 476, the western empire was brought down by Germanic peoples.

[Outro]
The Western Roman Empire, after centuries of expansion and decline, thus came to an end.
The Western Empire fell, but Rome's legacy still lives strongly in the law, language, architecture, and political system of Europe today.

lessons.style: Atmospheric cinematic synth-pop, 84 BPM, glassy pads, soft mallets, delicate arpeggiators, piano, and slowly widening strings. A sense of discovery, scale, and quiet wonder. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The human brain weighs about 1.3 kilograms.
Though only a tiny part of the body in weight, inside it lies a network of 86 billion neurons.
Each neuron is linked with thousands of others through synapses.

[Verse 2]
In the whole brain, around 100 trillion synapses form a netlike network.
Memory, perception, emotion, judgment.
Everything we call self arises from this complex neural activity.

[Verse 3]
How consciousness arises from the matter of the brain — this is one of the greatest mysteries of science.
Since the late twentieth century, imaging technology such as functional MRI has allowed researchers to directly observe the brain in action.

[Bridge]
What part of the brain becomes active when we see something, when we remember something — these can now be tracked in real time.
One recent discovery is the plasticity of the brain.

[Verse 4]
Once, it had been believed that the adult brain no longer changed.
But it is now known that the connections between neurons continue to change throughout life through new experience and learning.
Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and stroke.

[Outro]
Treatments for those who suffer from brain diseases or brain injuries are still being studied around the world.
To draw out, to its fullest, the power of the brain's recovery.
Brain research leads us toward the deepest question we may ever ask: what is a human being?

lessons.style: Cinematic folk-orchestral song, 82 BPM, piano, acoustic guitar, measured frame drums, cello, and gradually expanding strings. Historical scale without bombast, with a reflective present-day perspective. Build historical tension without turning revolution into a triumphant battle song. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
At the end of the eighteenth century, France was suffering from a serious financial crisis and famine.
Heavy taxes weighed on peasants and the urban poor, while the gap between ordinary people and the royal court of Louis XVI and Marie Antoinette at Versailles was simply too great.

[Verse 2]
The thought of the Enlightenment philosophers Voltaire and Rousseau had already spread among the educated class.
Liberty, equality, and the dignity of the human person.
These ideals would become the trigger of the revolution.
On July 14, 1789, the citizens of Paris stormed the Bastille prison.

[Verse 3]
This became the starting point of the French Revolution.
In August of the same year, the National Assembly adopted the Declaration of the Rights of Man and declared that all people held equal rights.
In 1793, Louis XVI was executed by the guillotine.

[Bridge]
France was transformed from a monarchy into a republic.
But in the middle of the revolution, the Jacobins under Robespierre carried out the Reign of Terror, and tens of thousands were executed as enemies.

[Verse 4]
In 1799, the young soldier Napoleon Bonaparte took power in a coup, and the chaos of the revolution came to an end.

[Outro]
He would become emperor in 1804, but the reform that the revolution brought — equality before the law, freedom of religion, the protection of private property — spread throughout Europe.
Liberty, Equality, Fraternity.
The three ideals of the French Revolution still flow at the foundation of every democratic society in the world today.

lessons.style: Atmospheric cinematic synth-pop, 84 BPM, glassy pads, soft mallets, delicate arpeggiators, piano, and slowly widening strings. A sense of discovery, scale, and quiet wonder. Begin almost weightless and expand gradually into a vast cosmic soundscape near the final lines. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In 1929, the American astronomer Edwin Hubble discovered that the more distant a galaxy was, the faster it was moving away from us.
This showed that the entire universe was expanding.

[Verse 2]
If the universe is expanding now, then in the past everything must have been small, hot, and gathered into a single point.
From this idea, the theory of the Big Bang was born.
Today, the universe is believed to have begun about 13.8 billion years ago, in the Big Bang.

[Verse 3]
In its first few minutes, hydrogen and helium were created, and over hundreds of millions of years, the first stars ignited.
In 1965, the American researchers Penzias and Wilson detected weak microwave radiation coming evenly from every direction of the sky.

[Bridge]
This is called the cosmic microwave background, and it is regarded as the afterglow of the Big Bang.
It became decisive evidence for the Big Bang theory.
Our Milky Way galaxy is said to hold between 200 and 400 billion stars.

[Verse 4]
In the universe, there are said to be roughly roughly the same number of galaxies.
But 95 percent of the universe still remains a mystery to us.
Dark matter, which we cannot directly observe, and dark energy, which is accelerating the expansion of the universe.

[Outro]
To uncover the nature of these is the greatest challenge of modern physics.
The James Webb Space Telescope, launched in 2021, is now bringing to us the light of the earliest galaxies of the universe.
Light born 13.8 billion years ago is finally reaching the Earth.

lessons.style: Cinematic folk-orchestral song, 82 BPM, piano, acoustic guitar, measured frame drums, cello, and gradually expanding strings. Historical scale without bombast, with a reflective present-day perspective. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In the latter half of the eighteenth century, an event began in Britain that would transform society and the economy from its foundation.
It was the dawn of the Industrial Revolution.
The steam engine, improved by James Watt, transformed the very concept of power.

[Verse 2]
Manufacturing, which had until then depended on rivers or on horses, could now run twenty-four hours a day on the power of coal and machines.
In Manchester and Liverpool, huge cotton textile factories were built one after another.

[Verse 3]
People who had until then worked the land in the countryside moved into the urban centers in search of work.
Urbanization advanced rapidly during this time.
But the labor conditions in the factories was terrible.

[Bridge]
Workdays of more than twelve hours, low wages, and children forced to work in the mines and the factories.
Child labor was the dark side of the society of that age.

[Verse 4]
After the middle of the nineteenth century, workers began to organize unions and to strike for better treatment.
Through the efforts of social reformers, laws limiting child labor were passed one after another.

[Outro]
The Industrial Revolution greatly raised living standards and the average lifespan of humanity.
At the same time, it brought deep gaps between rich and poor, and serious environmental pollution.
Our society today still lies on the path of the transformation that the revolution began.

lessons.title: H071 — 文学とは何か
lessons.style: Sophisticated cinematic art-pop, 92 BPM, expressive piano, elegant strings, clean bass, and lightly asymmetric percussion. Visually evocative, emotionally mature, and rhythmically clear. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Throughout history, across every land, humanity has continued to tell stories.
Literature is one of the oldest forms of expression in which human beings have written down and passed on their understanding of themselves.

[Verse 2]
The epic of Homer, the plays of Shakespeare, the long novel of Tolstoy, the Tale of Genji of Murasaki Shikibu.
Each literary work passes on to us how the people of its age looked at the world.
Why is literature important?

[Verse 3]
Because literature lets us live the lives of people other than ourselves, almost as if it were our own.
By living through the joy, the sadness, and the conflicts of the characters, we widen our own world.
Soseki's Kokoro, Dostoyevsky's Crime and Punishment.

[Bridge]
These novels shine light even on the dark parts of the human heart.
Literature often holds out, face to face, the questions we wish to turn away from.
Poetry, too, is an important part of literature.

[Verse 4]
With few words, it catches the essence of a single moment.
Through metaphor and symbol, a poem reaches directly into the depths of our hearts.
Even now, when films and the internet fill our days, why does literature not vanish?

[Outro]
Perhaps because the experience of reading a book quietly, alone, is itself an irreplaceable time when we converse with ourselves.
The quiet dialogue that arises between reader and writer is the true power of literature.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Japan is one of the most earthquake-prone nations in the world.
It lies in a region where plates overlap in a complex way, and hundreds of tremors are observed every year.
On March 11, 2011, a massive earthquake struck the Tohoku region.

[Verse 2]
At magnitude 9.0, it was one of the largest ever recorded.
The tsunami that followed swept the coasts of Iwate, Miyagi, and Fukushima, taking the lives of about twenty thousand people.

[Verse 3]
At the Fukushima Daiichi nuclear plant, the earthquake and tsunami caused the loss of cooling function, and a serious accident — a meltdown — occurred.
Hundreds of thousands of people were forced to evacuate the land they had long called home.

lessons.title: H073 — 人体と健康
lessons.style: Hopeful ambient pop, 88 BPM, clear piano motif, warm pads, acoustic-electronic percussion, and soft strings. Respectful and resilient, never sensational or melodramatic. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The human body is an astonishingly complex system made up of about thirty-seven trillion cells.
The heart beats about 100,000 times a day, and the lungs breathe in and out about 20,000 times a day.

[Verse 2]
The food we eat is digested in the stomach and intestines, and is delivered as energy to tissues throughout the body.
Nutrients such as protein, vitamins, and minerals are essential for the body's repair and growth.

[Verse 3]
The three pillars of staying healthy are said to be moderate exercise, a balanced diet, and sufficient sleep.
When these are broken, the risk of various diseases rises.
Lack of exercise can cause heart disease and diabetes.

[Bridge]
Too much salt or sugar leads to high blood pressure and obesity.
Lack of sleep weakens the immune system and makes a person more likely to fall ill.
Stress affects not only mental health, but also physical health, in serious ways.

[Verse 4]
Chronic stress can cause digestive trouble, headaches, sleeplessness, and depression.
Regular medical checks help to detect disease early.
Physicians listen to a patient's lifestyle and, when needed, suggest a treatment.
The body is the most precious tool that has been given to each of us.

[Outro]
The small choices of each day support a long life.
Health is not something we attend to only on special occasions, but something that lives in the daily fabric of our lives.

lessons.title: H074 — 伝統と祭り
lessons.style: Warm world-folk art-pop, 92 BPM, acoustic strings, piano, hand percussion, and carefully restrained regional color. Respectful, contemporary, and never novelty music or caricature. Add distant festival bells and hand drums, used sparingly and without a cartoon tone. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In every region of the world, there is a ritual or a festival unique to that land.
They reflect the people's view of the world, their sense of religion, and their relationship with nature.

[Verse 2]
In Japan, the first shrine visit of the year, Setsubun, Obon, and the festivals of each region are still carefully kept.
The Gion Festival of Kyoto has a history of more than a thousand years, and the Nebuta Festival of Aomori fills the night streets with passion.

[Verse 3]
Such traditions are not merely a habit of the past.
It is also a place where the people of a community confirm their own identity — who they are.
In the world, there are rites of passage that celebrate birth, adulthood, marriage, and death.

[Bridge]
These are events in which the whole community stands beside a person at a turning point of life and sends them on toward a new stage.
But the wave of globalization is making the unique cultures of each place uniform.

[Verse 4]
Young people move to the cities, and the bearers of local festivals continue to decline.
Many traditional crafts have already disappeared.
On the other hand, there is also a movement to preserve such fading cultures.
UNESCO registers the traditional cultures of various regions of the world as intangible heritage.

[Outro]
Japanese food, Noh theater, and the making of Japanese paper are among these.
Tradition is not a relic of the past.
It is a living gift that we, the people who live now, hand down to the next generation.
