lessons.title: H075 — 言葉と翻訳
lessons.style: Warm world-folk art-pop, 92 BPM, acoustic strings, piano, hand percussion, and carefully restrained regional color. Respectful, contemporary, and never novelty music or caricature. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
There are said to be about seven thousand languages spoken in the world today.
Each language reflects the way the people who speak it see the world.
Translation is the work of rebuilding the meaning of one language in the words of another.

[Verse 2]
But it is not a simple replacement of words.
For example, Japanese expressions such as mottainai, the phrase used before a meal, and otsukaresama cannot be literally translated into English.
These words have the culture and sensitivity of Japan deeply embedded in them.

[Verse 3]
Conversely, English words like serendipity, nostalgia, and privacy are also hard to replace with a single Japanese word.
Each language has its meaning within its own cultural context.
The translation of poetry is one of the most difficult challenges.

[Bridge]
To recreate, in another language, the rhythm, the sound, and even the silence between the lines of a poem is nearly impossible.
Even so, translators devote long hours to bring the spirit of the original back to life in another tongue.

[Verse 4]
In recent years, the accuracy of machine translation by AI has improved rapidly.
Google Translate and DeepL greatly help our daily communication.
But the translation of cultural nuance and literary beauty is still the work of the human translator.

[Outro]
Translation is the act of building a bridge between two worlds.
Even if no translation is perfect, as long as the work continues, we draw a little closer to one another's hearts.

lessons.title: H076 — 移民と多文化社会
lessons.style: Thoughtful cinematic indie pop, 88 BPM, steady 4/4, warm piano, brushed drums, subtle bass pulse, and restrained low strings. Dignified documentary mood that gradually opens toward hope. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Why do people leave the land where they were born?
War, poverty, persecution.
Or the wish for a better life.
The reasons vary, but the decision to leave one's homeland is difficult in every age.
From the nineteenth to the twentieth century, millions of Europeans crossed the ocean to America.

[Verse 2]
Families traveled together on long voyages, and a new life would begin.
Upon arrival, immigrants first suffered from the barrier of language.
Without a single acquaintance, lonely days went on.
Many could barely afford the cost of passage.
The actual life in America was far harder than they had imagined.

[Verse 3]
Low wages, poor housing, and discrimination.
Still, many immigrants gradually adjusted to the new society.
Their children learned English at school and blended into the local community.
Becoming accustomed to their new surroundings, they began to build lives of their own.

[Bridge]
At the same time, immigrants also kept the cultures of their ancestors.
Food, music, festivals.
Their diversity enriched the society that received them.
Today, cities around the world have become multicultural societies.
For different cultures to coexist, tolerance toward one another and the effort to overcome prejudice are needed.

[Outro]
Whether a society can turn diversity into strength depends on everyone who lives in it.

lessons.title: H077 — メディアリテラシー
lessons.style: Thoughtful cinematic indie pop, 88 BPM, steady 4/4, warm piano, brushed drums, subtle bass pulse, and restrained low strings. Dignified documentary mood that gradually opens toward hope. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Every day, we are exposed to an enormous amount of information.
Newspapers, television, articles on the internet, and posts on social media.
But how much of it is truly accurate?
An advertisement exists not simply to convey facts, but to encourage purchases.

[Verse 2]
Political propaganda manipulates information in order to spread a particular viewpoint.
Now anyone can publish information on social media.
As a result, unverified rumors and misleading information spread instantly.
The more sensational the headline, the more attention it draws.
What, then, should we believe?

[Verse 3]
First, verify the source of the information.
Who published it, and what evidence does it rest upon?
If statistics are quoted, examine critically how that data was gathered.
It is also important to compare several sources for any single event.

[Bridge]
If we judge from only one perspective, we arrive at a biased conclusion.
Critical thinking is the only power that protects us in this sea of information.
Media literacy has become an essential skill for everyone living in our age.

[Outro]
It is not about doubting all information, but about facing information in the right way.

lessons.style: Organic cinematic folk-pop, 86 BPM, acoustic guitar, felt piano, airy strings, gentle woodwinds, and natural percussion. Spacious, observant, and emotionally grounded, with a subtle rise in the final section. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
On Earth, an estimated 8.7 million species exist.
But it is said that of those, one million are now facing the threat of extinction.
The greatest cause is the destruction of habitat through human activity.

[Verse 2]
Deforestation, conversion to farmland, urbanization.
The places where animals live are being rapidly lost.
Poaching is also a serious problem.
Elephant ivory, rhino horn, tiger fur.
Illegal trade continues around the world.
Climate change is making the problem worse.

[Verse 3]
The rise in sea temperature has caused the bleaching of coral reefs, and if the Arctic ice melts, polar bears will lose their hunting ground.
The environment is being rapidly altered.
But there is also hope.

[Bridge]
Governments and NGOs have established protected areas and are running breeding programs for endangered species.
Scientists monitor population numbers and create conservation plans based on careful assessment.

[Outro]
Biodiversity is the foundation that supports our food, our medicine, and our planet's climate.
To protect it is, in the end, to protect ourselves.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In 1969, humanity reached the moon.
More than fifty years later, the goals of space exploration are set even farther away.
The next goal is Mars.
NASA is advancing plans to carry out a crewed mission to Mars in the 2030s.
Private companies, too, have entered space development in earnest.

[Verse 2]
SpaceX has developed a reusable rocket, greatly lowering the cost of launch.
But the journey to Mars is full of obstacles.
The distance from Earth to Mars, even at its closest, is about 55 million kilometers.
During the six-to-nine-month trip, astronauts are exposed to radiation, microgravity, and psychological isolation.

[Verse 3]
For humans to live on Mars, the supply of oxygen, water, and food is essential.
In the future, a colony is envisioned in which water is extracted from underground and crops are grown in greenhouses.
Space exploration comes at an enormous cost.

[Bridge]
Some argue that the budget should instead be used to solve problems on Earth.
But supporters argue that space exploration creates technological innovation and brings new solutions to Earth's problems as well.
Space will remain the last frontier for humanity.

[Outro]
The challenge of going there is not only a matter of science.
It is also a philosophical question: how far can humanity go?

lessons.style: Spacious chamber-pop, 78 BPM, felt piano, cello, subtle ambient texture, and minimal percussion. Reflective, intimate, and intellectually calm, leaving breathing room between ideas. Let the piano phrases feel like questions and answers, with meaningful pauses after rhetorical questions. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Philosophy begins with doubting what we take for granted.
What is justice?
What is a good life?
What can we know?
These questions have been asked since ancient Greece, 2,500 years ago, to the present day.

[Verse 2]
Plato argued that beyond the visible world there lay a perfect world of Ideas.
Aristotle thought that we could approach truth only through concrete experience.
The contrast between the two became the archetype of the history of philosophy.

[Verse 3]
In the seventeenth century, Descartes wrote his famous words, I think, therefore I am.
Even if one doubts everything, the existence of the self that doubts cannot be doubted.

[Bridge]
This became the starting point of modern philosophy, and the problem of consciousness was placed at the center.
Kant asked what a moral act truly was.
He said, Ask yourself whether the principle of your action could become a principle for all.

[Verse 4]
He tried to set the standard of good and evil in an absolute way.
Nietzsche doubted the very system of existing moral values.
His declaration God is dead was a radical question thrown at a modern society whose traditional values had collapsed.

[Outro]
In philosophy, the act of continuing to ask has more meaning than finding an answer.
To face an abstract question is the most fundamental act by which we come to deeply understand who we are.

lessons.style: Expansive cinematic folk-rock, 106 BPM, driving acoustic guitar, clean electric guitar, live drums, and broad strings. A steady feeling of movement, courage, and discovery. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The history of exploration is also the history of humanity being drawn toward places not yet seen.
At the end of the fifteenth century, Columbus crossed the Atlantic and reached the Americas.

[Verse 2]
In the sixteenth century, the fleet of Magellan achieved the first circumnavigation of the world.
Many sailors lost their lives, but their voyage rewrote the map of the world.

[Verse 3]
In the twentieth century, the stage of exploration shifted to the poles, the highest mountains, the deep sea, and the sky.
In 1911, Amundsen of Norway was the first to reach the South Pole.

[Bridge]
About a month later, the British team of Scott arrived, but all perished on their return.
It was a story of endurance and sacrifice in a harsh environment.
In 1953, Edmund Hillary and Tenzing Norgay became the first to stand on the summit of Everest.

[Verse 4]
Their determination showed how strong the human spirit could be against the most difficult obstacles.
The expedition of Ernest Shackleton is another story still told today.

[Outro]
His ship was trapped in ice, with no rescue in sight, yet he brought every member of his crew back alive.
It was leadership and courage pushed to the extreme.
Today, exploration heads toward the deep sea, outer space, and the limits of the human body.
Why do people try to cross the boundary?
Perhaps because the question itself — what lies beyond — is what makes us human.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
A small electronics company was founded thirty years ago in a regional city.
The founder was a capable engineer whose commitment was stronger than anyone's.
In the first years, the company carried debt.
The figures in the accounts were discouraging, and revenue was small.

[Verse 2]
But he convinced investor after investor and raised funds little by little.
In time, the company rose in the competitive market.
It won contracts with overseas clients and rode the wave of expansion.
As chairman, the founder spoke to every employee at the annual conference.

[Bridge]
Our strength is not strategy, but the sincerity of each person, he said.
Today, the company enjoys commercial success while never forgetting its contribution to the local community.
Transparency in management, fairness in how employees are promoted.

[Outro]
The story of this small firm teaches us that business success cannot be measured by numbers alone.

lessons.style: Sophisticated cinematic art-pop, 92 BPM, expressive piano, elegant strings, clean bass, and lightly asymmetric percussion. Visually evocative, emotionally mature, and rhythmically clear. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Cinema is one of the newest of all the arts, born at the start of the twentieth century.
In just over a hundred years, film has become the center of all entertainment.
The power of cinema lies in recreating a story before our eyes.

[Verse 2]
A dramatic scene shakes the heart of the audience, and a comedy creates laughter.
A great film presents social issues in a way that fascinates and makes the viewer think.
By retelling historical events from a creative angle, it delivers emotional truth that a textbook cannot.

[Verse 3]
Film critics evaluate a work from many sides.
Awards such as the Academy Awards have served to make the quality of films known to the world.
Watching a film is not mere amusement.
In a dark theater, we relive the life of another.

[Bridge]
What impresses us is not only the beauty of the images.
It is because the choices and conflicts of the characters throw questions at our own way of living.
In the digital age, the way films are made and watched has changed.

[Outro]
But the essence — to move the human heart through story — has not changed one bit since cinema was born with such enthusiasm a century ago.

lessons.style: Organic cinematic folk-pop, 86 BPM, acoustic guitar, felt piano, airy strings, gentle woodwinds, and natural percussion. Spacious, observant, and emotionally grounded, with a subtle rise in the final section. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The world population has passed eight billion.
Yet more than 800 million people still lack enough food and suffer from hunger.
Agriculture is one of the oldest industries of humanity and a foundation of civilization.

[Verse 2]
Since the invention of irrigation farming in ancient Mesopotamia, humanity has multiplied crop yields many times over through improved varieties and new technology.
In the Green Revolution of the twentieth century, high-yield varieties and chemical fertilizers dramatically increased food production in Asia and Africa.

[Verse 3]
But at the same time, the excessive use of pesticides and fertilizers has contaminated soil and water, causing long-term problems.
In recent years, both organic farming and genetically modified crops have drawn attention.

[Bridge]
The former is kinder to the environment but difficult for mass production; the latter raises yields but leaves concerns about safety.
Another major problem is food waste.
In developed countries, about one third of all food produced is thrown away.

[Verse 4]
In a world where people go hungry, this is a serious contradiction.
Solving the food problem requires more than increasing production.
Improvement in distribution, reduction of waste, and a change in the awareness of each consumer are all needed.

[Outro]
To feed the world in a sustainable way is the greatest challenge of the coming century.

lessons.style: Thoughtful cinematic indie pop, 88 BPM, steady 4/4, warm piano, brushed drums, subtle bass pulse, and restrained low strings. Dignified documentary mood that gradually opens toward hope. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In the world today, there are still children who cannot receive even elementary education.
In sub-Saharan Africa and South Asia, absence and dropout are serious problems.
What blocks access to education?
Poverty, conflict, geographical isolation, and gender inequality.

[Verse 2]
Families unable to pay school fees, villages where children must walk for hours to reach a school, customs that deny girls the right to attend.
These disadvantages create deep inequality.
Yet many studies have shown that education is the most effective tool for breaking the cycle of poverty.

[Verse 3]
An educated woman tends to raise healthier children and to earn a higher income.
The United Nations has set the goal, quality education for all by 2030.
Through scholarships, the spread of digital learning, and the training of teachers, each country pursues its own path toward achievement.

[Bridge]
With the spread of tablets and the internet, even remote areas are gaining access to educational content.
Technology can be a great force in closing the gap in education.
Education has the power to change not only the life of a single person but the whole of society.

[Outro]
That is why investment in education is the most efficient investment in the future.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The rule of law is the principle that all people are equal before the law and that no power holder may stand above the law.
This principle, which began in ancient Rome, forms the foundation of modern democratic society.

[Verse 2]
A constitution stands as the supreme law, and every other law is placed beneath it.
In the real world, however, there are many countries where the rule of law does not work well enough.

[Verse 3]
Corruption spreads, and those in power sometimes twist the law to their own advantage.
Judges may come under political pressure and lose the ability to make independent decisions.

[Bridge]
A person who commits a crime is brought to trial, and if found guilty, is confined.
But in recent years, the purpose of punishment has been shifting from mere penalty toward rehabilitation.

[Verse 4]
The aim is to help former prisoners return to society and to prevent them from falling back into criminal conduct.
Citizens, too, carry the responsibility of taking part in upholding the law.

[Outro]
When citizens raise their voices against wrongdoing and demand transparency of the system, they support the health of democratic society.
Law is the promise of a society.
The will to keep that promise, and to reform it as needed, is what builds the foundation of a free and just society.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
One morning, the alarm rang, but I was not eager to get up — I was simply bored.
I had been annoyed by the same routine repeating itself every day.
I tried to make coffee, but the beans had run out.

[Verse 2]
I walked to the neighborhood cafe and ordered coffee from a clerk I knew by sight.
I had no cash, so I paid by card.
On the way back, I met the elderly lady next door.

[Verse 3]
Yesterday I lost my precious ring in the garden, she said.
An insect bit my hand, and when I waved it, the ring flew off.
I did not mind helping.
I was glad to help.

[Bridge]
After digging for fifteen minutes with a shovel, a golden ring appeared from the soil.
She laughed and said, What good luck you bring, young man.
Back at home, a friend called.
Will you come camping next week?
he asked.

[Verse 4]
I accepted the invitation at once.
I would need to borrow a tent.
A day I had thought would be boring turned out, by the end, to be a good day blessed by circumstance.

[Outro]
In the ordinary flow of daily life, small events and conversation are always waiting.
Perhaps every day is, after all, a little more comfortable than we think.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
On a stormy night, a strange sound came from the ceiling of an old mansion.
The master had disappeared from his study.
The door was locked from the inside, and the window was blocked by a brick wall.

[Verse 2]
The inspector who received the report rushed to the scene.
He walked through the long corridor and entered the study.
The room was nearly empty.
Only a shelf fixed to the wall seemed out of place.

[Verse 3]
But he did not dismiss it.
Behind the shelf, there was an entrance to a hidden passage.
The inspector did not hesitate and went in.
The dark corridor led underground.
In the basement, the master had been captured.

[Bridge]
The criminal was his former business partner.
A financial dispute had been the motive.
The inspector immediately managed to identify the suspect.
A clear motive, physical evidence, and a discarded key mechanism all pointed to him.

[Outro]
The case was resolved in a single night.
The truth had been hiding in plain sight.

lessons.style: Thoughtful cinematic indie pop, 88 BPM, steady 4/4, warm piano, brushed drums, subtle bass pulse, and restrained low strings. Dignified documentary mood that gradually opens toward hope. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In a democratic nation, voting is one of the most fundamental civic acts.
Citizens regularly go to the polls and choose their representatives.
When the campaign begins, each candidate puts forward an agenda and appeals to the voters.
Healthcare, education, the economy, the environment.

[Verse 2]
Which issue to emphasize becomes the mark of each candidate.
Sometimes the election does not give a single party the majority.
In that case, several parties form a coalition and share power.
In a coalition government, compromise is essential.

[Verse 3]
The elected leader appoints cabinet members and leads each department of the federal government.
A new bill becomes law only after receiving approval from the legislature.
In recent years, interest in elections has declined in some countries.

[Bridge]
Turnout falls, and some young people ignore politics, saying, It has nothing to do with me.
But those who do not vote lose an important opportunity to shape the result.
Democracy functions only through the participation of its citizens.

[Outro]
Meanwhile, there are countries in the world where elections are not even held.
Advocates continue to call for the right of every person to vote.
Elections are not perfect, but they remain one of the most crucial tools we have.

lessons.title: H090 — 科学的方法
lessons.style: Atmospheric cinematic synth-pop, 84 BPM, glassy pads, soft mallets, delicate arpeggiators, piano, and slowly widening strings. A sense of discovery, scale, and quiet wonder. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Scientific inquiry begins with a question.
Why is the sky blue?
Why does metal conduct heat easily?
Within everyday doubt lies the seed of science.
A scientist first forms a hypothesis.
Then an experiment is designed to test it.
The conditions are carefully determined, and the equipment is prepared.

[Verse 2]
In the experiment, the factor that could affect the result is controlled as much as possible.
Only one factor is changed while the rest are kept constant.
This allows the researcher to distinguish whether the result was caused by that factor.

[Verse 3]
The data obtained are analyzed and compared with the hypothesis.
If the result supports the hypothesis, further testing follows.
If the hypothesis is rejected, a new explanation is sought.
The heart of the scientific method is that any conclusion is temporary.

[Bridge]
No matter how established a theory may be, there is always the possibility that new evidence will rewrite it.
It is this repeated process that has driven the progress of science.

[Outro]
From biological research to electronic engineering, each component is carefully examined, and the properties of each compound are described in an elaborate way.
Science is the work of an intelligence that never ceases to doubt.

lessons.title: H091 — 南ヨーロッパ旅行記
lessons.style: Sunlit acoustic pop with subtle bossa and world-folk hints, 102 BPM, nylon guitar, soft hand percussion, piano, and warm bass. Open, observant, and gently cinematic. Add understated Mediterranean nylon guitar and accordion colors without becoming tourist music. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The week after I graduated from university, I set off alone for southern Europe.
A cheap airline ticket and a worn-out backpack were all I had.
The old quarter of Barcelona was a maze of bare stone walls and narrow lanes.

[Verse 2]
My footsteps echoed against the walls.
At every turn, a small craft shop or a folk music bar appeared.
Down at the harbor, a dozen fishing boats were lined up.

[Verse 3]
In the market, the scent of fresh bread and the aroma of rich spices drifted in the air and stirred my appetite.
I took a train south and stayed at an inn in a whitewashed village.

[Bridge]
The owners were a generous elderly couple who served me dinner.
The furniture was old but well kept.
On the last morning, I leaned on the balcony and looked out at the sea.
The wind blew gently.

[Outro]
This time of leisure was exactly what I had been seeking on the journey.
The trip taught me something.
The world is far more friendly, and far broader, than I had ever imagined.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Freedom of expression is one of the essential pillars of democracy.
But how far should that freedom extend?
This is one of the most controversial questions in modern society.
Hate speech, discriminatory expression, and deliberate misinformation.
Should these fall within the range of free speech?

[Verse 2]
Many countries have placed limitations on forms of expression that cause harm.
On the other hand, regulation carries the danger of excess.
If a government controls expression too much, citizens become afraid and stop raising their voices.

[Verse 3]
Finding the balance between freedom and safety is extremely difficult.
The emergence of the internet has made this issue considerably more complex.
A statement posted on social media spreads instantly, and removing it is virtually impossible.
Activists continue to fight to protect freedom of expression.

[Bridge]
At the same time, there is a growing demand for laws that protect victims of harmful speech.
What matters most is the attitude of listening even to opinions that are contrary to one's own.
So long as we maintain dialogue, society can avoid division.

[Outro]
Freedom of expression is also the freedom to listen.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Modern people live more conveniently than ever before.
But at a cost, the health of body and mind tends to be neglected.
Lung function weakens without exercise, and muscle mass diminishes if not used.

[Verse 2]
A sedentary lifestyle becomes a factor in diabetes and heart disease.
The quality of sleep is also crucial.
Staring at a smartphone screen late at night exposes the brain to intense light, and sleep becomes shallow.

[Verse 3]
Consequently, the next day's concentration drops considerably.
On the mental side, the number of people carrying anxiety and depression is growing.
The more intense the competition in society becomes, the heavier the burden.

[Bridge]
What is necessary to maintain health is nothing special.
A thirty-minute walk each day, a balanced diet, seven hours of sleep.
And not hesitating to ask for help when in trouble.
Body and mind are inseparable.

[Outro]
If you move your body, your mind grows lighter.
If your mind is stable, your body will also recover.
Health is the accumulation of small daily habits.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
People spend much of their life at work.
An occupation is not merely a way to earn a living.
It is also a major factor that shapes who a person is.
A student graduates from university, applies for a position, and gets hired.

[Verse 2]
Under a new employer, the person begins working, associating with colleagues and superiors while learning the skills of the job.
But not everything goes smoothly.
One may fail.
If judged not suitable for the work, one may be fired.

[Verse 3]
Unemployment has a major impact not only on finances but also on mental health.
On the other hand, some people use their talent to start their own enterprise.
A venture involves risk, but it also holds potentially great rewards.

[Bridge]
More people are changing professions in the middle of their career.
In an age where people live to be a hundred, there is no need to cling to a single job.
One's priority changes at each stage of life.

[Outro]
What matters is to find meaning in one's work.
Satisfaction lies not in the size of a paycheck, but in the feeling that one is contributing to society.

lessons.title: H096 — 国際関係と外交
lessons.style: Thoughtful cinematic indie pop, 88 BPM, steady 4/4, warm piano, brushed drums, subtle bass pulse, and restrained low strings. Dignified documentary mood that gradually opens toward hope. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
International relations are a complex web between nations.
Alliances, treaties, and trade agreements form the framework that supports the order of the world.
But when the interests of nations conflict, tension rises.

[Verse 2]
Some nations turn to aggression, while others choose to negotiate.
After the two world wars of the twentieth century, the United Nations was established.
Its purpose was to resolve disputes peacefully through negotiation.

[Verse 3]
But the veto power of the Security Council has often become an obstacle.
During the Cold War, the world was divided into two opposite camps.

[Bridge]
The threat of nuclear weapons served as an overwhelming deterrent, but the world was constantly on the edge of crisis.
Even after the Cold War ended, new threats such as regional conflicts, terrorism, and cyberattacks have continued to emerge.

[Outro]
No problem can be resolved by one nation alone.
The work of a diplomat is to build bridges between opposing interests.
For nations that oppose one another to find mutual benefit — that is the ultimate objective of diplomacy.

lessons.style: Organic cinematic folk-pop, 86 BPM, acoustic guitar, felt piano, airy strings, gentle woodwinds, and natural percussion. Spacious, observant, and emotionally grounded, with a subtle rise in the final section. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
On Earth, there are more than 6,000 known species of mammals alone.
The number of insect species is estimated in the millions.
Tropical rainforests cover only about six percent of the Earth's surface, yet more than half of all species dwell there.
These hotspots of biodiversity are shrinking rapidly.

[Verse 2]
The causes are numerous.
Logging, conversion to farmland, urban development.
Human activity is steadily taking the habitat of animals away.
The oceans are also vulnerable.
Plastic pollution harms whales and turtles, and the chemicals carried by the tide threaten the food chain.
But conservation efforts are beginning to yield results.

[Bridge]
One Indigenous community has protected the forest of its ancestors and established a pioneering model of community-led conservation.
An ecosystem is built on a subtle balance.
The loss of one species affects others in a chain.

[Outro]
Whether we can find the wisdom to coexist with nature will determine the future of this planet.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In just thirty years, technology has entirely changed our daily life.
Electronic devices are beside us from the moment we wake until we sleep.
In the morning, the alarm rings and we check the news on a smartphone.

[Verse 2]
We pay for breakfast by electronic payment and are guided to the office by the navigation of our automobile.
At the office, equipment has been installed to handle vast amounts of data.

[Verse 3]
Meetings are held remotely, and documents are signed electronically.
The electrification of vehicles is expected to reduce exhaust emissions and make city air considerably cleaner.
Battery technology is being enhanced at a rapid pace.

[Bridge]
On the other hand, the problems of privacy loss and the digital divide are growing more serious.
To distribute the benefits of technology fairly has become an obligation of society.
Technology is something that enables, not something that rules.

[Outro]
Whether we master technology, or are dominated by it — that choice is always in our hands.

lessons.title: H099 — 人生と選択
lessons.style: Spacious chamber-pop, 78 BPM, felt piano, cello, subtle ambient texture, and minimal percussion. Reflective, intimate, and intellectually calm, leaving breathing room between ideas. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Life is a chain of choices.
From the small choice of what to eat in the morning, to the grave decision of what profession to follow or whom to live with.
We cannot always make the correct choice.

[Verse 2]
We make mistakes, and we feel regret.
But failure is often what brings the insight for the next step.
Fear often stops us.
What if I fail?
What if they laugh?

[Verse 3]
To overcome that fear and take a step forward is courage.
There is a word called fate.
But fate is not something determined in advance.
Through each daily decision, we determine our own path.

[Bridge]
A philosopher once said, Life can only be lived forward, but it can only be understood backward.
That may be precisely true.
What matters is to keep walking the road we have chosen.

[Outro]
Occasionally we stop, look back, and then walk on.
There is no guarantee in life.
But that is precisely why each day is precious.

lessons.style: Sophisticated cinematic art-pop, 92 BPM, expressive piano, elegant strings, clean bass, and lightly asymmetric percussion. Visually evocative, emotionally mature, and rhythmically clear. Use a spacious museum-like reverb and delicate musical colors that appear and disappear like paintings. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
That day, a special exhibition was being held at the museum.
Valuable paintings brought from Europe were being exhibited in Japan for the first time.
At the entrance I bought a ticket and walked along the route.

[Verse 2]
In the first room, portraits from the fifteenth century were on display.
The faces of kings and nobles, painted with a primitive yet powerful brushstroke.
The next room held Impressionist paintings.
Monet, Renoir, Degas.

[Verse 3]
Attempts to capture the light appeared, each with the personality of its artist.
I stopped before one painting and gazed at it for a long time.
Other visitors passed by, whispering.
Something the painting awakened remained with me.

[Bridge]
A female guide was explaining the historical background of the paintings to newly arrived students.
They were eagerly taking notes.
When I left the museum, I carried a profound satisfaction in my heart.

[Outro]
Art, across time and place, quietly brings relief to the heart of the viewer.
It is not a luxury, but one of the forms of nourishment that human beings need.

lessons.title: H101 — 裁判の一場面
lessons.style: Restrained noir trip-hop, 82 BPM, upright bass, brushed drums, low piano, subtle electronic pulse, and sparse strings. Suspenseful but not frightening, with exceptionally clear vocal phrasing. Keep a measured courtroom pulse and leave a short silence before the verdict line. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The court was silent.
The prosecutor rose and began to lay out the details of the case methodically.
The defendant was at the scene on the day of the crime.
This is definite from the testimony of several witnesses.

[Verse 2]
The defense attorney rose and argued back.
What seems apparent is not always the truth.
We have new evidence that will prove the defendant's alibi.
On the witness stand, a young woman was trembling.

[Verse 3]
She was the person who had provided several clues to the police.
Her testimony was crucial.
That night, I saw the defendant run from the scene, she answered in a voice close to a whisper.

[Bridge]
It was still too early for the judge to hand down his judgement.
Weeks later, the jury reached a verdict.
Guilty.
The defendant was sent to jail.
But the attorney decided to appeal.

[Outro]
Law must be strict, but it must not lose room for mercy.
The pursuit of justice is always also a confrontation with the limits of human judgement.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Behind the Olympics, there are countless stories the media does not show.
The stories of dedication carried by each athlete over many years.
Early in the morning, athletes gather at the training ground.
The one they compete against is often the people they were yesterday.

[Verse 2]
Consistent practice produces remarkable results.
At the opening ceremony, thousands of athletes march in.
They raise their national flags and exchange greetings in harmony.
For that moment alone, every nation becomes one.
During competition, an athlete sometimes suffers an injury.

[Verse 3]
Some keep running even while enduring pain.
In the figure of a runner giving everything, there is something beyond mere victory or defeat.
Athletes who did not win a medal return home to their families.

[Bridge]
Even in tears of disappointment, there is the resolve for the next attempt.
The true significance of the Olympics does not lie in the number of gold medals.
At the closing ceremony, athletes from every nation mingle as they enter.

[Outro]
Ethnicity and religion do not matter.
In that moment, sport teaches us that it is a common language of humanity, beyond words.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
On Sunday afternoon, I visited an old bookshop.
In a corner at the back of the store, wooden shelves reached up to the ceiling.
The owner was an elderly man with white hair.
He greeted me lightly and returned to his reading.

[Verse 2]
Inside the shop, only the sound of turning pages and the ticking of an old clock echoed.
I stopped before a shelf of poetry and picked up a volume.
The book had not been touched by anyone for a long time, and when I opened it, a peculiar scent rose.

[Verse 3]
As I turned the pages, I noticed a bookmark tucked inside.
An old handwritten note was on it.
I give this book to you.
June 1968, from Father.
I let out a sigh.

[Bridge]
A book once handed from a father to his son had traveled for more than half a century and was about to pass into my hands, a stranger.
I told the owner that I wanted to purchase the book.

[Outro]
He glanced at the note and, after a moment of silence, quietly remarked, This is something valuable.
Back home, I read the poems.
Outside, rain was gradually beginning to fall.
The words within the book, across sixty years, had reached me now.

lessons.style: Clean modern rhythmic indie pop, 96 BPM, muted electric piano, soft plucked synth, precise bass, and light electronic-acoustic drums. Intelligent, energetic, and easy to follow without sounding corporate. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
From 2022 onward, sharp inflation occurred across the world.
Energy prices, food, housing.
The price of everything rose considerably.
The causes were multiple.
Supply chain disruption due to the pandemic, Russia's invasion of Ukraine, large fiscal spending by governments.

[Verse 2]
These combined to create a tremendous rise in prices.
In response, central banks raised interest rates.
The borrowing cost for businesses and households rose, and consumption and investment cooled.
Many countries stood at the edge of recession.

[Verse 3]
The pain of rising prices is not equal.
Wealthy households hold assets and are relatively protected.
But for low-income families, food and utility costs become a burden that presses on daily life.
The national deficit has also grown.

[Bridge]
Social security expenses swell, and tax revenue alone cannot cover them.
Debt becomes an obligation to future generations.
The challenge of the economy cannot be solved by one country alone.

[Outro]
In our globalized age, international coordination is the foundation of a sustainable economy.

lessons.style: Intimate indie folk and piano ballad, 80 BPM, acoustic guitar, felt piano, cello, and very light drums. Warm, honest, and emotionally restrained, building to quiet hope rather than a huge climax. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Mr. Tanaka is seventy-two.
He retired five years ago from the company where he had worked for long years.
After his retirement, his days have passed slowly.

[Verse 2]
Early each morning, he goes out to the garden and waters the flowers his late wife had grown.
His wife passed away three years ago from a sudden illness.
He still remembers the day of the funeral vividly.

[Verse 3]
Every Sunday, he visits his wife's grave.
Before the stone, he joins his hands and quietly prays.
His silent prayer is carried away by the wind.
Mr. Tanaka carries many regrets.

[Bridge]
In his younger years, he had been consumed by work and had spent little time with his family.
His wife never complained, but in her late years she had whispered, I wish we had traveled more together.

[Verse 4]
Those words still linger in his heart.
Now, Mr.
Tanaka travels alone.
One by one, he visits the places his wife had wanted to see.
Somehow, he feels as if he is walking together with her.
The passage of life always comes quietly.

[Outro]
From youth to middle age, from middle age to old age.
And then, to farewell.
Mr. Tanaka, within the gently flowing time, spends his remaining days.
I want to finish the last chapter of my life quietly, he says.

lessons.style: Intimate indie folk and piano ballad, 80 BPM, acoustic guitar, felt piano, cello, and very light drums. Warm, honest, and emotionally restrained, building to quiet hope rather than a huge climax. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The institution of marriage has evolved with time.
Once it was mainly a bond between families, an alliance between houses.
Today, the love and choices of two individuals are the primary reason.
With each anniversary, a couple comes to know each other more deeply.

[Verse 2]
But not everything always goes well.
Conflict can accumulate, and an intimate relationship can grow cold.
The rate of divorce has been rising around the world.
It is not appropriate to see this only as a negative phenomenon.

[Verse 3]
It is also one aspect of a society that gives priority to the happiness of the individual.
The background of divorce is complicated.
Financial strain, differences in values, the burden of raising children.
It cannot be attributed to a single cause.

[Bridge]
When there are children, divorce becomes a particularly delicate issue.
A parent's choice has a substantial impact on a child's life.
Both parents carry the responsibility to consider the welfare of the child even after they part.
Neither marriage nor divorce has a single correct answer.

[Outro]
What matters is an attitude of mutual respect and honest engagement.
Whatever its form, a family remains an association of love.

lessons.style: Hopeful ambient pop, 88 BPM, clear piano motif, warm pads, acoustic-electronic percussion, and soft strings. Respectful and resilient, never sensational or melodramatic. Use a slightly faster 96 BPM pulse suggesting coordinated emergency work, without thriller exaggeration. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
At two in the morning, the corridor of the emergency department was silent.
Suddenly the sound of a siren drew near.
The victim of a traffic accident was being brought in.
The patient was a woman in her thirties.

[Verse 2]
She was conscious, but blood kept flowing from a deep wound.
The doctor on duty decided on an immediate operation.
The nurses, with practiced movements, prepared for surgery.
Medical devices, blood for transfusion, sterilized instruments.
Not a moment of delay could be allowed.

[Verse 3]
The surgery lasted three hours.
The doctor had to concentrate and, with the greatest care, stitch each blood vessel.
Not a single symptom could be overlooked.
Eventually the surgery ended, and the doctor wiped the sweat from his brow.
The patient's condition became stable.

[Bridge]
The family, in the waiting room, shed tears and thanked him.
Recovery will take time.
But she had been saved.
Doctors, nurses, technicians.
Through the teamwork of all the hospital personnel, a single life was saved.
In medical settings, such stories are repeated every day.

[Outro]
Under tremendous pressure, they continue their work.
Dedication is the greatest force that supports medicine.

lessons.title: H108 — 戦場の静けさ
lessons.style: Solemn cinematic chamber ballad, 74 BPM, low strings, sparse piano, distant ambient texture, and restrained percussion. Compassionate and anti-sensational, with no triumphant or militaristic feeling. Make silence part of the arrangement; no gunshot sound effects and no heroic military color. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
On the battlefield, there was a fear that no movie can convey.
An armed unit advanced through the forest.
Everyone held their breath.
Suddenly, from the front, the sound of a blast echoed.
The commander gave orders in a low voice.
Scatter.

[Verse 2]
Everyone, drop to the ground.
Bullets flew between the trees.
Combat began.
Beside a young soldier, a comrade fell.
A bloody scene spread before them.
Minutes later, the shooting stopped, and the area was wrapped in an uncanny silence.
The soldiers, trembling, rose to their feet.

[Verse 3]
Who had survived, who had been lost?
The tragedy of war is the accumulation of such moments.
Even the distinction between friend and enemy is sometimes lost in confusion.
Soldiers who return from the battlefield are haunted by those memories for life.

[Bridge]
Some develop PTSD or depression, and some are driven to suicide.
The wounds of war remain deep long after the shooting has stopped.
There are no winners in war, a veteran once said.
Both victory and defeat give birth to the same grief in the end.

[Outro]
Will the day ever come when humanity can truly abolish war?

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Japan's insurance system is one of the best in the world.
Every citizen is enrolled in public medical insurance, and can receive treatment at a fixed share of the costs.
What supports this system is monthly premiums and taxes.

[Verse 2]
The premium is automatically deducted from employees' salaries.
The self-employed belong to the National Health Insurance.
The system is complicated, and what is apparently simple actually consists of many provisions.
A particular provision defines the scope of benefits that a subscriber can obtain.

[Verse 3]
As the nation ages, medical and pension spending is rapidly increasing.
The premiums paid by the working generation alone cannot cover it, and the deficit has been growing.
Private insurance companies also offer a wide range of products.

[Bridge]
Cancer insurance, life insurance, personal pensions.
A buyer can choose according to his or her needs.
Insurance is preparation for an unpredictable future.
Anyone may, someday, face illness or an accident.

[Outro]
So that a household is not ruined at that moment, society as a whole pools funds — this is the essence of insurance.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
As individual human beings, each of us is very small.
The Earth lies in a corner of a galaxy, and the universe holds hundreds of billions of galaxies.
When we imagine that scale, human activity seems insignificant.

[Verse 2]
Yet at the same time, is it not astonishing that we can have consciousness and wonder about the universe?
Ancient philosophers looked up at the night sky and thought.
Why are we here?

[Verse 3]
Is there meaning for us, who are only one aspect of all this?
We too, under the night sky, can hold the same questions.
Modern science teaches us much.
The universe originated 13.8 billion years ago.
Stars generate energy by fusion.

[Bridge]
Life arose from chemical reactions.
But why does being exist, and why is there this universe rather than nothing?
Science has no definitive answer to this root question.
Human consciousness is also mysterious.

[Verse 4]
Why, from the electrical signals of neurons, do the sensation of red or the emotion of joy emerge?
Neither psychologists nor philosophers has yet given a clear answer.
To face these questions comes with a painful loneliness.

[Outro]
But it is also a privilege given only to human beings.
Though we are small, we can think about the universe itself.
Is there anything more extraordinary than this?

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
It was a spring morning when I learned that my wife was pregnant.
Along with joy, a great responsibility settled on my shoulders.
Nine months later, our infant was born.
Our son.
Small hands, small feet, a peaceful sleeping face.

[Verse 2]
Just by being there, the world seemed to change.
But raising a child was far tougher than I had imagined.
Babies cry regardless of day or night.
Frequently, we were kept busy with feeding and changing diapers.
Lack of sleep was severe.

[Verse 3]
Even when we desperately wanted sleep, the sound of his crying woke us immediately.
My wife and I were both exhausted.
And yet, the moment our son laughed, all the fatigue blew away.
The feel of his small hand gripping my finger.

[Bridge]
When I feel the heartbeat in his chest as he sleeps, I feel deeply happy.
Raising a child is also a process that makes a parent a parent.
While we seem to be raising the child, we are in truth being raised by the child.

[Verse 4]
Patience, endurance, unconditional love.
My son drew out of me qualities I had never possessed before.
A few years later, my son began attending nursery school.
Every morning, at parting, he waves his small hand.

[Outro]
The relationship between my son and me will develop over a long journey.
Until he is a teenager, until he is an adult, until one day he leaves home.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Regret may be a capacity that may be uniquely human.
Looking back on past choices and imagining if only I had done that is a notion that requires complex thinking.
In high school, I damaged a relationship with a girlfriend in my class.

[Verse 2]
In a trivial quarrel, I hurt her pride.
If only I had been more polite back then.
If only I had been able to perceive her feelings.
Unfortunately, the young me did not have that capacity.

[Verse 3]
On graduation day, she came up to me nervously, gave a short wave, and left.
After that, we lost touch.
It was mostly my responsibility.
Even after decades, I sometimes think of her.

[Bridge]
Through news from a mutual friend, I learned that she had built a happy family.
Along with relief, I also felt a faint sadness.
Regret is at times an unpleasant feeling.
But to confront regret is also part of growth.

[Outro]
We cannot change the past, but we can learn from it.
If I could go back, I would confidently tell her a simple thank you.
I am slowly forgiving my past self for not having said it.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Modern society is full of contradictions.
A person who is materially prosperous may still feel unhappy inside.
Why?
With the spread of social media, we have come to relate to others more than ever before.
But at the same time, chances to compare ourselves with others have also increased.

[Verse 2]
The lives of others look attractive.
Beautiful travel destinations, delicious meals, impressive achievements.
Inevitably, our own life comes to feel dull.
But what social media shows is only a portion of another's life, and at that, a deliberately chosen moment — the most glittering one.

[Verse 3]
Everyone, behind the camera, hides the fatigue and worries of daily life.
Psychologists indicate that excessive social media use can become the basis for depression and anxiety.
Especially for the young, especially for teenagers, the consequences are serious.
The answer is not to quit social media entirely.

[Bridge]
It is to keep our distance and turn our eyes to our own life.
To step away from the folly of comparing another's peak with our own average.
True happiness is not found in the comparison with others, but in a sense of self-acceptance.

[Outro]
To indeed realize this is the challenge of those of us who live in the modern age.

lessons.style: Spacious chamber-pop, 78 BPM, felt piano, cello, subtle ambient texture, and minimal percussion. Reflective, intimate, and intellectually calm, leaving breathing room between ideas. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
A large social experiment revealed something about human nature.
Someone would lose a wallet and a stranger would find it.
The experiment was to assess whether the wallet was returned.
The result was astonishing.

[Verse 2]
Conducted in public places in more than forty countries, the more cash the wallet contained, the higher the percentage of return.
At first glance this seems odd.
With more money, the temptation to keep it should be greater.
But humans typically strongly dislike thinking of themselves as a thief.

[Verse 3]
The behavior of taking the money upsets one's self-image.
The greater the amount, the greater the psychological cost.
So, on the contrary, the rate of return rises.
This experiment suggests that people care about others and about seeing themselves as honest.

[Bridge]
It fundamentally challenges the notion, long presumed by economists, that people act only out of self-interest.
Of course, there are exceptions.
Crime is not zero.
But overall, the majority of people are honest and wish to help others.
This fact brings us relief.

[Outro]
The wrongdoing we see in the news stands out, but the quiet goodness of daily life supports the world.
Trust in humanity can rest on evidence from ordinary life.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Correspondents reporting from war zones play a vital role in informing us of what is happening in the world.
Journalists who go to conflict areas stake their own lives to convey the truth.
They are constantly exposed to danger.

[Verse 2]
Via satellite phones and the internet, their images and words are transmitted around the world instantly.
From our living room, we witness a distant battlefield in a visible form.
But the truth of war is not only what is shown on camera.

[Verse 3]
Much pain is invisible and cannot be conveyed on screen.
The sadness of refugees who have lost their homes, the suffering of children deprived of safety and education.
Among journalists, some sadly lose their lives on the ground.

[Bridge]
In the war in Ukraine since 2022 alone, many reporters have been killed.
They have become victims of murder, accidents, and attacks.
Even so, they continue their reporting.
Why?
Because they carry the conviction that if the truth is not told to the world, the same tragedy will happen again.

[Outro]
To protect the freedom of the press is to protect democracy.
And to the journalists who continue to report the truth at great risk, we cannot help feeling we owe something.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
My grandfather was a man who hardly spoke.
He seldom talked about himself, and rarely showed his emotions openly.
When I was young, that confused me.
What was he thinking?
Did he dislike me?

[Verse 2]
But as the years passed, I came to understand him.
His silence was not coldness, but a quiet love.
The generation that lived through the war tends to avoid talking about it.
Remembering itself causes pain.
They touch the past only briefly.

[Verse 3]
After my grandfather passed away, I found notebooks he had been writing.
In them, his detailed memories of the battlefield, and his private feelings about his family, were recorded in small handwriting.
He had truly loved us.

[Bridge]
It was simply difficult for him to put it into words.
For him, love was shown through action.
Tilling the field with me on his day off, secretly sending a small gift on his grandchild's birthday.

[Verse 4]
Inside my grandfather's silence, I grasped true kindness.
His silence did not mean that words were useless — rather, there was a love that went beyond words.
On my late grandfather's birthday, I go to his grave to offer flowers.

[Outro]
I briefly join my hands in prayer and quietly speak to him for a short time.
My grandfather, even now, in an invisible form, lives within my heart.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The society of the twenty-first century faces unprecedented complexity.
Climate change, pandemics, economic crises, political division.
There is no longer any problem that a single country can cope with on its own.
To face these extraordinary challenges, international cooperation is indispensable.

[Verse 2]
But in reality, each nation often gives priority to its own interests.
Global interdependence has deepened than ever.
A financial crisis in one country spreads across the world in an instant.
An infectious disease in one region crosses continents in weeks.

[Verse 3]
In such an interconnected world, it makes no sense to distinguish between us and them.
The suffering of someone will, in time, become the suffering of someone else.
For the sake of future generations, we need a firm commitment.
Effective action against climate change, initiatives to end poverty, efforts toward peace.

[Bridge]
What one individual can do looks small at first glance.
But when the choices of billions of individuals gather, the world surely changes.
Daily consumption, voting, posts on social media.
These are all votes that shape the future.
Hope is not optimism.
Hope is a commitment to action.

[Outro]
No matter how harsh the circumstances, to keep moving for a better future.
That is the small and great responsibility of each one of us.

lessons.style: Thoughtful cinematic indie pop, 88 BPM, steady 4/4, warm piano, brushed drums, subtle bass pulse, and restrained low strings. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In modern society, immigration is a topic that cannot be avoided.
The number of people moving across borders has continued to rise significantly.
Receiving countries show various reactions.
Some welcome immigrants, others reject them.
Politicians often turn this issue into a political point of dispute.

[Verse 2]
The challenges that immigrants pose are multiple.
Language, culture, religion, and economy.
Friction between the receiving society and new immigrants may occur.
But looking back at the history of immigration, we see that they have made many contributions to their receiving countries.

[Verse 3]
The prosperity of America was built by immigrants from around the world.
There is also wide variation among immigrants.
Some move voluntarily for economic reasons; some flee war or persecution as refugees; some come to reunite with family.
They cannot be grouped together.

[Bridge]
The welcoming attitude of a society has a great effect on the integration of immigrants.
In a society that coldly rejects newcomers, immigrants become isolated and sometimes turn to extremism.
What solves this most effectively is education and dialogue.

[Outro]
A society that does not fear difference but learns from it.
That is the key that opens the twenty-first century.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
My grandfather is eighty-four.
He began to paint ten years ago.
After retirement, he had time on his hands and wanted to focus on something.
In his youth, he had been convinced that he had no talent for painting.

[Verse 2]
An art teacher in middle school told him, You are bad at painting.
You are better suited for music.
Since then, he had not touched a brush.

[Verse 3]
But after retirement, he happened to stand before a painting in a museum and thought he wanted to paint too.
Already seventy-four, the family worried that he was too old to begin.
Yet he joined a local painting class.

[Bridge]
People of various ages came to the class, but he was the oldest.
At first he was shy, but he gradually found joy in it.
Ten years on, his works hang on the walls throughout the house.

[Verse 4]
He has even held a small exhibition at a local gallery.
His grandchildren treasure his paintings as their favorite.
He says, Age has nothing to do with beginning something.
Creation keeps a person young.
My grandfather's hand, when he holds a brush, does not tremble.

[Outro]
The act of painting calms his nerves and sharpens his focus.
Art may be a powerful answer to the challenges of old age.
It is never too late to begin something.
My grandfather's example demonstrates this to me.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Words have potential.
A single word can destroy a person, or save one.
The problem of bullying has long been a concern of society.
In schools, at workplaces, and on the internet.
Not only visible violence, but also the violence of words carries serious implications.

[Verse 2]
Children are particularly vulnerable.
Ugly.
Stupid.
You should die.
Words thrown casually can cut deeply into a child's heart.
Slander on social media intensifies through anonymity.
Under malice sent daily by invisible senders, many young people are pushed to the edge of their mental limits.

[Verse 3]
Some die by suicide.
Words have consequences.
We are recently rediscovering this truth.
What was meant as a light joke may hurt the other like a blade.
But words also carry the power to heal.
Thank you.
It's okay.
You are not alone.

[Bridge]
Such words can lift someone who is about to collapse.
Indeed, words are both a weapon and a medicine.
Which one they become depends on the choice of each one of us.
Today, pay attention to the words you speak.

[Outro]
What can you offer to lighten someone's heart?

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The sea ice of the Arctic is rapidly melting.
The evidence shown by satellite photos is shocking.
What was once white is giving way to blue ocean, one area after another.
Scientists had not predicted such rapid change.

[Verse 2]
Ten years ago, models had estimated that the kind of ice retreat we see now would happen around 2050.
But reality is advancing at a pace far beyond the prediction.
The primary cause is the emission of greenhouse gases from human activity.

[Verse 3]
At the same time, melting land ice and warming oceans are raising sea levels.
Small Pacific island nations such as Tuvalu and Kiribati are already facing the crisis of being submerged.
Their residents may eventually be forced to leave their homelands.

[Bridge]
The Arctic has its own unique ecosystem — polar bears, Arctic foxes, seals.
If the ice disappears, these animals lose their habitat and face the threat of extinction.
Even more serious is the release of vast amounts of methane gas that had been trapped in the permafrost.

[Verse 4]
This has many times the warming effect of carbon dioxide and accelerates warming.
Governments have set up committee after committee, and representatives debate countermeasures.
But reaching agreement to contain the problem is not easy.
The Earth is the home of all of us.

[Outro]
It is not someone else's problem.
If we do not act now, what will be destroyed is the dwelling of future generations.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Dogs descended from wolves some fifteen thousand years ago.
Through living with humans, they acquired roles as hunters, guards, and companions.
In modern times, dogs play various roles.
Guide dogs, police dogs, therapy dogs.

[Verse 2]
They are intelligent, sensitive, and perceive human emotions with surprising accuracy.
Scientists have demonstrated that dogs read human facial expressions and show distinct emotional responses.
When an owner is sad, the dog seems sad.

[Verse 3]
When an owner is happy, the dog wags its tail.
Pet therapy, which eases the loneliness of the elderly, has also been gaining attention in recent years.

[Bridge]
For an elderly person living alone, a dog becomes a member of the family and a daily source of meaning.
But keeping a dog also comes with responsibility.
Food, medical costs, time for walks.

[Verse 4]
One must be prepared for a commitment of fifteen years or more.
Sadly, there are owners who make excuses and abandon their animals.
Not a few dogs are sent to shelters and may never find new homes.

[Outro]
To take an animal as family is to carry responsibility to the end.
Those who cannot must never treat them as disposable.
The bond between dogs and humans is a special one, nurtured over thousands of years.
We should protect this bond by caring for animals responsibly.

When an owner is sad, the dog seems sad.

sections.name: Verse 3
lines: When an owner is happy, the dog wags its tail.
Pet therapy, which eases the loneliness of the elderly, has also been gaining attention in recent years.

sections.name: Bridge
lines: For an elderly person living alone, a dog becomes a member of the family and a daily source of meaning.
But keeping a dog also comes with responsibility.
Food, medical costs, time for walks.

sections.name: Verse 4
lines: One must be prepared for a commitment of fifteen years or more.
Sadly, there are owners who make excuses and abandon their animals.
Not a few dogs are sent to shelters and may never find new homes.

sections.name: Outro
lines: To take an animal as family is to carry responsibility to the end.
Those who cannot must never treat them as disposable.
The bond between dogs and humans is a special one, nurtured over thousands of years.
We should protect this bond by caring for animals responsibly.

lessons.title: H123 — ゴッホの沈黙
lessons.style: Sophisticated cinematic art-pop, 92 BPM, expressive piano, elegant strings, clean bass, and lightly asymmetric percussion. Visually evocative, emotionally mature, and rhythmically clear. Add expressive art-rock guitar swells like brushstrokes, but keep the core intimate and compassionate. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The artist Van Gogh could barely sell any of his paintings during his lifetime.
He was rejected and criticized by ordinary people and experienced severe mental distress.
Just before he took his own life at thirty-seven, he had sold only one painting.

[Verse 2]
Without the support of his brother Theo, he could not even have bought paint.
Despite all this, Van Gogh created about 2,100 works in ten years.
Paintings and drawings, an enormous number together.
His dedication was not in pursuit of success.

[Verse 3]
Decades after his death, his paintings began to be reevaluated.
Today, Sunflowers and The Starry Night are counted among the most popular paintings in the world.
They are traded for billions of yen each.
While Van Gogh was alive, few people recognized his potential.

[Bridge]
His brother Theo was one of the few exceptions.
Theo believed in his brother's talent and, at considerable sacrifice, kept supporting him.
Van Gogh's story asks about the definition of success.
Is success to be recognized in life?
Is success to be recognized after death?

[Verse 4]
Perhaps, for Van Gogh himself, success was to keep painting.
Whatever the reaction of the world, he kept painting according to his inner voice.
That was the integrity of his life.
We can see the truth of a human being in the canvases Van Gogh left behind.

[Outro]
Colors that seem to yell, a life force that seems to burst.
Instead of staying silent, he continues to speak to the world through his paintings.

lessons.title: H124 — 成功の再定義
lessons.style: Spacious chamber-pop, 78 BPM, felt piano, cello, subtle ambient texture, and minimal percussion. Reflective, intimate, and intellectually calm, leaving breathing room between ideas. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The notion of success has changed with the times.
Once, to rise in a big company and retain a stable position was the typical description of success.
But today, the younger generation has come to hold different preferences.

[Verse 2]
Rather than an expensive car or house, there is a stronger inclination toward free time and meaningful work.
Freelance work, starting a business, remote work.
New ways of working have gained in popularity.
People have begun to seek values that cannot be measured by salary alone.

[Verse 3]
Sociologists call this change a shift in values.
Resistance to labels and status has grown, and the happiness and health of the individual have become the prime concern.
Nevertheless, it is not easy to completely abandon the conventional view of success.

[Bridge]
The expectation of the parents' generation, the pressure of society, one's own unease.
What matters is to achieve a life where we feel we are living as ourselves, rather than success as described by others.
Success is to live according to one's own values.

[Outro]
This may be the definition of success for the twenty-first century.
To walk the rough road of life with our own feet.
That is where truly satisfying fulfillment lies.

lessons.title: H125 — 詐欺と自衛
lessons.style: Restrained noir trip-hop, 82 BPM, upright bass, brushed drums, low piano, subtle electronic pulse, and sparse strings. Suspenseful but not frightening, with exceptionally clear vocal phrasing. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The methods of fraud are becoming more sophisticated year by year.
Phone calls, emails, social media.
Criminals cleverly target human vulnerabilities.
Especially the it's me, it's me fraud, which targets the elderly, has been a social issue for years.

[Verse 2]
The caller pretends to be a relative and claims things like I caused a traffic accident or I took money from the company.
The victim, shaken, loses normal judgment.
Told please send the money immediately, they do as instructed.

[Verse 3]
Sometimes the caller pretends to be a police officer or a bank agent.
They warn your account has been used fraudulently and try to obtain your password or verification code.
Even if told your family is in trouble, first calm down.

[Bridge]
Immediately call the family member directly to confirm.
If the phone number is not identical, be suspicious.
Banks and government offices never ask for personally sensitive information by phone.
If you are asked, it is almost certainly fraud.

[Verse 4]
If you are a victim, some people feel shame and cannot talk to anyone.
But it is important not to carry it alone.
Police hotlines and consumer centers can provide help.
Fraudsters exploit human kindness and goodwill.
The feeling for my family is precious.

[Outro]
But do not let that feeling prevent you from pausing to verify the facts.
With sensible judgment and action, you can protect both yourself and your family.

lessons.title: H126 — 桜と日本人
lessons.style: Warm world-folk art-pop, 92 BPM, acoustic strings, piano, hand percussion, and carefully restrained regional color. Respectful, contemporary, and never novelty music or caricature. Add very subtle koto-like plucked texture and bamboo flute color within the modern arrangement. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In spring, the cherry blossoms begin to open.
Last winter was especially harsh, and many people were anxious, waiting for the blossoms.
Cherry blossoms are a special flower for the Japanese.

[Verse 2]
Since ancient times, they have been written into poems, drawn in paintings, and have become a feature of the culture.
The custom of holding a flower-viewing party under the cherry trees has a history of more than a thousand years.

[Verse 3]
When we see the cherry trees in full bloom, everyone holds their breath.
The sight of petals dancing in the wind is astonishing in its beauty.
But the beauty of the cherry blossom lies in its brevity.

[Bridge]
In about a week, the flowers fall.
The petals pile on the ground like a carpet.
That scene, too, has a unique beauty.
In Japanese culture, cherry blossoms represent mono no aware — a quiet sadness and love toward that which inevitably fades.

[Verse 4]
Because the time of bloom is short, it feels all the more beautiful.
Life, too, is as fleeting as cherry blossoms.
A decade, looking back, passes in an instant.
Youth, health, time with loved ones — none of it will last forever.

[Outro]
That is why we should cherish this moment, right now.
Under the cherry trees, to speak with friends, laugh with family, and quietly look up at the sky alone.
The sum of such small moments is life itself.
The cherry trees bloomed again this year.
Next year, and the year after, I want to see as many cherry blossoms as I can.
That simple wish is what keeps us alive.
