lessons.title: H127 — 防災と備え
lessons.style: Uplifting indie pop-rock, 108 BPM, clean electric guitars, firm live drums, melodic bass, and a cinematic lift. Energetic and motivational while keeping every English word clearly intelligible. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In Japan, a country of disasters, preparing for earthquakes and typhoons that may come at any time is indispensable.
Strengthening buildings and preparing evacuation plans have become standard responsibilities for national and local governments.
Preparation at home is also important.
Emergency food, water, flashlights, a well-maintained portable radio.

[Verse 2]
Keep these in an accessible place.
Children must be taught how to behave when an earthquake strikes.
First drop, cover your head, and hold on under a sturdy desk.
After the shaking stops, turn off flames if it is safe to do so.

[Verse 3]
So that you do not evacuate barefoot, keep shoes by the bedside.
Deciding where the family will gather is also important.
If people are scattered at school, workplace, and home, where will you meet?

[Bridge]
If this is not decided in the initial stage, you may be unable to contact one another in the confusion.
As a mental preparation for disasters, there is a concept called normalcy bias.
People want to think, I will be fine.

[Verse 4]
Even when a heavy rain evacuation order is issued, they think it's still fine and fail to escape in time.
To overcome this, accept that if nothing happens, that is good, and evacuate early.
Take actions that you hope will prove unnecessary.
That instinct saves lives.

[Outro]
Disaster preparation is a matter of planning and habit.
The accumulation of small daily preparations becomes a great difference when the moment comes.
Better safe than sorry.
This old proverb remains an unchanged truth.

lessons.title: H128 — 自動運転の未来
lessons.style: Forward-looking cinematic synth-pop, 100 BPM, warm arpeggiated synth, piano, rounded electronic bass, and clean hybrid drums. Curious and human rather than robotic, with controlled futuristic color. Use a precise motor-like pulse that softens whenever human responsibility is discussed. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
A driver's license is a symbol of adult status in many countries.
The freedom to drive one's own car and go anywhere.
It is an aspiration for many young people.
But driving comes with great responsibility.

[Verse 2]
A car is a convenient tool, but with a single wrong judgment, it can become a weapon that takes a life.
The result of a wrong maneuver can be fatal.
In recent years, self-driving technology has advanced rapidly.

[Verse 3]
The age is coming when AI handles many driving tasks, and the human operator is placed in a passive position.
There are five levels of autonomous driving.
Currently, most cars are around Level 2.

[Bridge]
They are at the stage of assisting some functions, such as lane keeping and automatic braking.
Fully autonomous driving, level 5, is still under development.
Whether AI can make smarter decisions than a human in complex traffic and traffic jams is still open to debate.

[Verse 4]
In the case of an accident, who is responsible?
The driver, the carmaker, or the AI developer?
Current law has not caught up with this new phase.
If autonomous driving spreads, the number of traffic deaths is expected to decrease.

[Outro]
Accidents caused by human inattention, fatigue, or drunk driving could be reduced, although AI introduces risks of its own.
But at the same time, many taxi and truck drivers may lose their jobs.
Technological progress is inevitable, but we must keep thinking about how society adapts.

lessons.title: H129 — ミツバチを守る
lessons.style: Organic cinematic folk-pop, 86 BPM, acoustic guitar, felt piano, airy strings, gentle woodwinds, and natural percussion. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Bees are one of the most important partners for humanity.
They fly from flower to flower, carrying pollen.
Without this work, many crops do not bear fruit.
One-third of the food grown in the world depends on pollinators such as bees.

[Verse 2]
The richness of our table is supported by the work of small bees.
But in recent years, the number of bees has been decreasing around the world.
The causes are complex.
Pesticides, the destruction of habitat, climate change, parasites.
Especially serious are pesticides containing neonicotinoids.

[Verse 3]
These chemicals interfere with the nervous system of bees and cause them to lose their sense of direction.
Bees that cannot return to the hive are isolated and eventually die.
The EU has banned the use of these pesticides.
Other countries are gradually strengthening restrictions.

[Bridge]
But there is also strong opposition to regulation.
Farmers worry that yields may fall without effective alternatives.
What must be weighed is agricultural productivity against environmental protection.
Citizens can also act.
Plant plenty of flowers in the garden and provide bees with nectar.

[Verse 4]
Buy honey from local beekeepers.
Try gardening without pesticides.
Bees function within the network of the ecosystem.
If they disappear, many organisms will be affected throughout the food chain.
In the end, the food security of humanity itself comes under threat.

[Outro]
A small being supports a great world.
To protect bees is to protect our own future.

lessons.style: Sophisticated cinematic art-pop, 92 BPM, expressive piano, elegant strings, clean bass, and lightly asymmetric percussion. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Across time and space, music has always been with humanity.
In the age when cave paintings were drawn, people were already playing instruments.
Flutes made of bone, drums with stretched skins.
Though primitive, it was certainly music.
Music has a mysterious power.

[Verse 2]
Even between people who do not share a language, melody and rhythm reach the heart directly.
Across dialect and borders, music, like a universal language, connects people.
Ancient Greek philosophers regarded music as a branch of mathematics.

[Verse 3]
They thought the proportion and harmony of sound reflected the order of the universe.
It may sound like a fancy theory, but today's science too continues to describe the laws of music.

[Bridge]
On the other hand, modern neuroscience has shown that music stimulates multiple regions of the brain simultaneously.
Hearing, movement, memory, emotion.
Few activities activate the brain as comprehensively as music.
Music therapy is employed even with patients with dementia and depression.

[Verse 4]
Even those who have lost their words, when they hear a song familiar from their youth, their expressions may return.
Music education should be highlighted in the growth of children.
Through learning an instrument, concentration, cooperation, and expression are nurtured.

[Outro]
But in recent years, school music education has been shrinking.
Budget restrictions is the main reason.
With the development of digital technology, an age has come when anyone can create music and share it with the world.
This is wonderful.
But at the same time, music has also come to be treated as mere consumer goods.
Music exists not for efficiency, but for the nourishment of the heart.
Within our busy days, let us keep time to listen attentively to music, even one song a day.
That is what keeps us human.

lessons.title: H131 — 父と海
lessons.style: Intimate indie folk and piano ballad, 80 BPM, acoustic guitar, felt piano, cello, and very light drums. Warm, honest, and emotionally restrained, building to quiet hope rather than a huge climax. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
My father, who was born and raised in a fishing village, has lived with the sea.
He would set out before dawn and judge the changing weather with care and support the family.
When my father was young, fish were abundant.

[Verse 2]
In the morning fishing, the nets would fill with silver fish.
Dealers waited at the port, and prices were set by auction.
But over the decades, the situation changed greatly.
The amount of fish in the sea kept decreasing.
The causes are complex.

[Verse 3]
Overfishing, ocean pollution, climate change.
At first, my father insisted that the old methods are enough.
His desire to preserve the conventional way of fishing was strong.
But changes in the times cannot be resisted.

[Bridge]
I, his son, introduced my father to new technology — fish finders and medium-sized seine nets.
My father, at first, resisted this mechanization.
But once he tried it, he was surprised at the efficiency.
Fishing methods must evolve, he came to say with a laugh.

[Verse 4]
But efficiency alone is not sustainable.
At the same time, we established closed fishing zones and made sure not to take too much.
Based on relevant scientific evidence, we monitor the fish population and aim for sustainable fishing.

[Outro]
My father now passes his experience on to younger fishermen.
So that the bounty of the sea reaches the generation of our children and grandchildren.
That is the shared wish of my father and me.

lessons.style: Solemn cinematic chamber ballad, 74 BPM, low strings, sparse piano, distant ambient texture, and restrained percussion. Compassionate and anti-sensational, with no triumphant or militaristic feeling. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
When I was in middle school, I was bullied.
Going to the classroom was a horror.
When the alarm rang in the morning, tears would pour out.
The incident that triggered it was so small that no one could guess.

[Verse 2]
At the school sports day, my team lost a relay match and finished last.
From there, one teammate began to blame me, and gradually the atmosphere of the class changed.
Garbage was placed inside my desk.

[Verse 3]
My gym uniform was dumped into the toilet.
No one would speak to me.
When I reported the matter to a teacher, I was dismissed with, It's merely teasing.
I was too embarrassed to confess to my parents.

[Bridge]
A sense of shame made me carry it alone.
One day, I simply could not go to school.
My mother at first showed anger, but seeing my face, she understood everything.
Working with the school, my homeroom teacher was changed.

[Verse 4]
Several classmates came to apologize to me.
I still remember the weight of the words, I am truly sorry.
Bullying eats at the heart of not only the victim, but also the one who bullies.

[Outro]
One of those who had bullied me contacted me years later.
I have been regretting it all this time, he said.
The wound has not completely disappeared.
But that experience made the person I am today.
A person who knows weakness can be kinder to another's weakness.
The experience of suffering can become a strength that may someday relieve someone else.
Now, as a teacher, I keep telling children, You are not alone.

lessons.title: H133 — 憲法と民主主義
lessons.style: Thoughtful cinematic indie pop, 88 BPM, steady 4/4, warm piano, brushed drums, subtle bass pulse, and restrained low strings. Dignified documentary mood that gradually opens toward hope. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In a democratic nation, the constitution functions as the supreme law.
All laws are placed under it, and laws that violate it are declared unconstitutional and invalid.
The Japanese Constitution came into force in 1947.

[Verse 2]
Because it was drafted under foreign occupation, there is criticism that it is an imposed constitution.
At the same time, it is also a fact that it has supported the peace and prosperity of postwar Japan.

[Verse 3]
Amendment requires the support of two-thirds of the Diet and a national referendum.
For this reason, it has never once been amended.
Debate over constitutional revision has continued for many years.
The focus is Article 9, the clause renouncing war.

[Bridge]
Supporters argue that amendment is needed to deal with the changing security environment.
Opponents insist that pacifism must be retained.
Poll results have swung with the times.
There is a survey suggesting younger generations tend to support revision, but among the elderly, more cautious opinions are common.

[Verse 4]
The debate over revision requires intellectual honesty.
Rather than vaguely wanting to change or vaguely wanting to preserve, we should discuss specific articles and a specific vision of the nation.

[Outro]
The constitution does not belong to any one group; it is born and can be changed through the will of the people.
Democracy functions only through the participation of each citizen.
The debate over the constitution is the most fundamental dialogue that decides the future of our nation.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
My family is raising eight-year-old twin daughters, Emma and Sophia.
Their resemblance is striking, but their personalities are characteristically different.
Emma is logical and thinks about things in an orderly way.
She is good at math and science, and she often devises puzzles to entertain the family.

[Verse 2]
Sophia, on the other hand, is sensitive and artistic.
She draws, sings, and reads out the stories she has made up to the family.
Even adults can be astonished at her power of expression.

[Verse 3]
Genetically, identical twins share nearly the same genes, yet as they grew, each one's personality has become more and more distinct.
This provides an interesting reference for studies of nature versus nurture.
Genes alone do not determine personality.

[Bridge]
Environment, experience, and the person's own choices shape each one.
If even twins differ, of course every human is unique.
What matters in raising a child is respecting each one's personality.
Making Emma draw the same picture as Sophia is pointless.

[Verse 4]
Making Sophia solve the same puzzle as Emma is painful.
The parents' role is to cultivate each child's strengths.
But parents are not the only ones who raise excellent human beings.
School teachers, friends, local community.
And the child's own effort.
Altogether, they shape a single person.

[Outro]
Emma and Sophia are growing up today, quarreling and laughing.
As they grow up, what kind of adults will they become?
As a parent, I am eagerly looking forward to it.

She is good at math and science, and she often devises puzzles to entertain the family.

sections.name: Verse 2
lines: Sophia, on the other hand, is sensitive and artistic.
She draws, sings, and reads out the stories she has made up to the family.
Even adults can be astonished at her power of expression.

sections.name: Verse 3
lines: Genetically, identical twins share nearly the same genes, yet as they grew, each one's personality has become more and more distinct.
This provides an interesting reference for studies of nature versus nurture.
Genes alone do not determine personality.

sections.name: Bridge
lines: Environment, experience, and the person's own choices shape each one.
If even twins differ, of course every human is unique.
What matters in raising a child is respecting each one's personality.
Making Emma draw the same picture as Sophia is pointless.

sections.name: Verse 4
lines: Making Sophia solve the same puzzle as Emma is painful.
The parents' role is to cultivate each child's strengths.
But parents are not the only ones who raise excellent human beings.
School teachers, friends, local community.
And the child's own effort.
Altogether, they shape a single person.

sections.name: Outro
lines: Emma and Sophia are growing up today, quarreling and laughing.
As they grow up, what kind of adults will they become?
As a parent, I am eagerly looking forward to it.

lessons.title: H135 — 千年の温泉
lessons.style: Warm world-folk art-pop, 92 BPM, acoustic strings, piano, hand percussion, and carefully restrained regional color. Respectful, contemporary, and never novelty music or caricature. Add subtle Japanese ambient-folk color: soft wooden percussion, plucked strings, and spacious water-like reverb. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In the early hours of a winter morning, steam appears on the mountainside.
The steam rising from the roof of a hot spring inn melts into the cold air.
This hot spring town has a history of more than a thousand years.

[Verse 2]
The water of the hot spring, referred to in old documents, still flows unchanged from the ground.
The innkeeper is the fifth generation of his family.
Rising early, he adjusts the temperature of the hot spring and prepares to welcome guests.

[Verse 3]
His measured manner of speech carries the sense of history that has accumulated in this land.
Guests come from across the country and from overseas.
Their dialects vary, but the moment they step into the bath, everyone lets out a deep breath in the same way.

[Bridge]
The relaxation of a hot spring is beyond words.
Soaking in the bath, I look out at the snowy scene through the window.
On distant mountains, snow has piled up, and the branches of trees are dyed white.

[Verse 4]
Here, far from the noise of the city, the flow of time slips into a gentle pace.
Dinner features dishes made with the ingredients of this land.
Wild mountain vegetables, river trout, soup made with local miso.
It is a taste one cannot find in the city.

[Outro]
After dinner, the innkeeper recites old stories.
Tales of the village's spirits, of gods, of ancestors.
They are not written in history books, but have been passed down orally as the memory of this land.
As the night deepens, only the sound of the water is heard.
The hot spring, welling endlessly from its source, flows on beyond the human scale of time.
A thousand years ago, now, a thousand years from now.
The waters of this land will keep healing people, unchanged.

lessons.title: H136 — 政治と金
lessons.style: Thoughtful cinematic indie pop, 88 BPM, steady 4/4, warm piano, brushed drums, subtle bass pulse, and restrained low strings. Dignified documentary mood that gradually opens toward hope. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The relationship between politics and money has been, across time and place, an enduring issue of democracy.
A politician swears to represent the will of the voters.
But in reality, they are bound by the source of campaign funds.

[Verse 2]
Whether Democrat or Republican, political activity costs large sums of money.
Campaigns, advertising, staff salaries.
Where to obtain these funds becomes the issue.
Corporate donations have long been a subject of dispute.
If a company donates money, it expects policies favorable to that company.

[Verse 3]
Corporate support may therefore carry an implied expectation.
Cases of corruption and bribery have brought down many ministers and lawmakers.
The anger of the public demands strict punishment for corrupt politicians.
Countries implement political fund laws.

[Bridge]
A maximum ceiling on donations, the duty of disclosure, examination of how money is spent.
But methods that circumvent the regulatory net keep being developed.
Political funding organizations and fundraising events can create many loopholes.
To ensure true democracy, the setting up of institutions alone is inadequate.

[Outro]
Public scrutiny, investigative reporting of the media, and the involvement of voters are indispensable.
For a vote to carry meaning, citizens must also accept the responsibility of watching politics closely.

lessons.title: H137 — 緑の革命
lessons.style: Atmospheric cinematic synth-pop, 84 BPM, glassy pads, soft mallets, delicate arpeggiators, piano, and slowly widening strings. A sense of discovery, scale, and quiet wonder. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In the 1960s, the poverty of developing countries was a problem that many developed nations preferred to ignore.
In many countries of Africa, Asia, and South America, hunger and disease caused people to suffer.
But an agricultural scientist took action.
Norman Borlaug.

[Verse 2]
He led a movement called the Green Revolution and, through the improvement of wheat varieties, succeeded in dramatically increasing the world's food production.
The high-yield varieties he discovered performed well in areas with limited rainfall.
In India and Mexico, wheat production doubled in a few years.

[Verse 3]
Hundreds of millions of lives were saved.
His achievement received worldwide recognition.
He received the Nobel Peace Prize in 1970.
The Green Revolution looked like a miracle, but there was also criticism.
Monoculture agriculture is vulnerable to pests.

[Bridge]
The use of chemical fertilizers drains the soil and lowers productivity over the long term.
Borlaug himself faced these criticisms sincerely.
The Green Revolution is only a temporary victory, he said.
As long as the population keeps growing, the food problem will not end.

[Verse 4]
Today, the world population has passed eight billion.
Without the achievements of the Green Revolution, hunger would be far worse.
But new challenges are piling up.
Climate change, depletion of water resources, soil exhaustion.
Next-generation technologies such as gene-edited crops are being developed.

[Outro]
But these technologies bring new ethical issues along with them.
Food security is a high-priority issue that every government must confront.
We must pass the lessons Borlaug left us on to the next generation.

lessons.title: H138 — チャップリンと無声映画
lessons.style: Sophisticated cinematic art-pop, 92 BPM, expressive piano, elegant strings, clean bass, and lightly asymmetric percussion. Visually evocative, emotionally mature, and rhythmically clear. Add elegant silent-film piano gestures and light pizzicato strings without turning comedic. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The birth of cinema was a miraculous invention at the end of the nineteenth century.
Since the Lumiere brothers held a public screening in Paris in 1895, film has become one of humanity's major art forms.
Early films were silent.

[Verse 2]
The story had to be conveyed through the actors' facial expressions and gestures alone.
The greatest star of that era was Charlie Chaplin.
Chaplin was born in 1889 to a poor family in London.

[Verse 3]
His father died young from alcoholism, and his mother suffered mental illness.
At seven, Chaplin was sent to an orphanage.
His childhood was a battle against awful poverty.
He survived on simple soup and stale bread.
But that experience gave depth to his later work.

[Bridge]
At twenty-five, Chaplin crossed to Hollywood and invented the character of the Tramp.
A bowler hat, a cane, a tiny mustache, shoes too big.
This figure was loved around the world.
His films were comedies, yet they sharply depicted the contradictions of society.

[Verse 4]
Modern Times satirized the alienation of industrial society; The Great Dictator satirized Nazi Germany.
In the 1950s, however, when the Red Scare began in the United States, Chaplin was suspected of being a communist sympathizer.
He left the US and went into exile in Switzerland.

[Outro]
In his later years, Chaplin's reputation was restored.
At the 1972 Academy Awards, the entire audience stood up and gave him a standing ovation.
The prolonged applause became one of the most memorable moments in Oscar history.
Chaplin's films do not fade even today.
Life is a tragedy when seen up close, but a comedy from a distance.
His words touch the truth of the human condition.

lessons.title: H139 — 火星移住の夢
lessons.style: Forward-looking cinematic synth-pop, 100 BPM, warm arpeggiated synth, piano, rounded electronic bass, and clean hybrid drums. Curious and human rather than robotic, with controlled futuristic color. Use a broad futuristic atmosphere and a hopeful but unresolved final chord. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Space development was once an undertaking carried only by nations.
But in the twenty-first century, private companies have entered one after another, and the commercial space age has arrived.
A leading company is Elon Musk's SpaceX.

[Verse 2]
It developed reusable rockets and dramatically reduced launch costs.
It achieved, in the private sector, technology at the same level as national space programs.
Mars colonization too, rather than a work of science fiction, has entered a concrete stage.

[Verse 3]
A giant rocket called Starship aims for a crewed Mars flight in the 2030s.
But in practice, the challenges pile up.
The one-way trip to Mars is six to nine months.
Cosmic radiation, osteoporosis, psychological isolation.

[Bridge]
To solve these problems requires many years of research.
Even when one arrives on Mars, the environment is unsuited to life.
The atmosphere consists mainly carbon dioxide, and temperatures are below zero.
Water freezes, and plants do not grow.

[Verse 4]
Even so, humanity keeps taking up the challenge.
Why?
There is no single answer, but the scientist Carl Sagan said, Earth is only a small dot.
By living on multiple planets, humanity increases its chances of survival.

[Outro]
There are also those opposed to Mars colonization.
It would only pollute a new planet without solving Earth's problems.
The vast funds should be used to end poverty.
There is a legitimate basis for this criticism.
Space development expands the possibilities of humanity.
But at the same time, we must not forget the responsibility to care for the Earth.
When we look up at the sky, we must direct our eyes to both the future and the present.

lessons.title: H140 — 60歳で英語を始めた母
lessons.style: Intimate indie folk and piano ballad, 80 BPM, acoustic guitar, felt piano, cello, and very light drums. Warm, honest, and emotionally restrained, building to quiet hope rather than a huge climax. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
My mother began studying English at sixty.
Having been a homemaker for many years, she made the decision when her grandchild was born.
At first, she struggled even with pronunciation.

[Verse 2]
Trying to make sounds her mouth was not used to, she would stretch her lips again and again.
She patiently corrected herself from reading tap as tapu.
But my mother was determined.

[Verse 3]
She would get up at six every morning and listen to English lessons on the radio.
After breakfast, she would read the textbook for an hour, committing the words to memory.
After half a year, she could handle simple daily conversation.

[Bridge]
After a year, she gave directions to a tourist.
After three years, she wrote an English essay at a university extension course.
My mother's progress was somewhat slow, but steady.
The secret was keep doing it every day.

[Verse 4]
Even a short amount of time, continued for 365 days, becomes a vast sum of hours.
When her grandchild turned five, she began speaking English with him.
The grandchild was amused to see his grandmother speak English.
Then, he too began learning English.

[Outro]
My mother's story teaches me something important.
Too late is only an excuse.

lessons.title: H141 — 日本人はなぜ長寿か
lessons.style: Hopeful ambient pop, 88 BPM, clear piano motif, warm pads, acoustic-electronic percussion, and soft strings. Respectful and resilient, never sensational or melodramatic. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Japanese people are among the longest-lived in the world.
The average lifespan is eighty-seven for women and eighty-one for men, at the world's top level.
What is the secret?
Many researchers have tried to uncover this mystery.
The first factor is diet.

[Verse 2]
Traditional Japanese food includes vegetables, fish, fermented foods, rice, and miso.
These are balanced in nutrition and do not contain excessive fat.
The second factor is lifestyle habits.
Japanese walk every day.
Even in cities, they commute by public transportation and walk to the station.

[Verse 3]
The elderly also keep walking as a habit.
The third factor is social connection.
As in Okinawa's yuimaaru, local communities are strong, and people are not isolated.
Okinawa especially is a well-known land of longevity, with many people over a hundred.

[Bridge]
The fourth factor is ikigai — a reason for living.
Japanese people have the concept of ikigai.
To hold small goals and daily enjoyments.
After retirement, they occupy themselves with a vegetable garden or devote themselves to calligraphy.
But long life has its shadows too.

[Verse 4]
Dementia, nursing care, and the burden on social security.
The challenge is not only to live long, but to simultaneously extend healthy life expectancy.
Young people today live differently from their parents' generation.
Fast food, greater reliance on cars, and increasingly international diets.

[Outro]
Will the next generation be able to maintain the same longevity?
Traditional food, the habit of walking, connection with community.
These are not old things, but a resource for the future.
To incorporate old wisdom into convenient modern life is the key to maintaining a long and healthy life across generations.
The secret of longevity is not a special medicine.
It is the accumulation of small daily choices.

lessons.title: H142 — ガラスの天井を越えて
lessons.style: Thoughtful cinematic indie pop, 88 BPM, steady 4/4, warm piano, brushed drums, subtle bass pulse, and restrained low strings. Dignified documentary mood that gradually opens toward hope. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Mariko, my university classmate, became the first woman to serve as factory manager at a major manufacturer.
It was when she was forty.
She had graduated from the engineering department and at first worked as a technician.

[Verse 2]
The workers on the floor were all men, and at first she was not accepted as a peer.
Mariko learned everything from the safety procedures on the shop floor to the operating methods of each machine.

[Verse 3]
She wore the same clothing as the workers and walked the factory from morning till night.
After ten years, she climbed the steps of promotion, becoming section chief, department head, and then factory manager.
This was unusual in the industry.

[Bridge]
Despite Mariko's appointment as factory manager, there were voices of both support and objection.
Can a woman, with a home and children to raise, carry such a responsible post?
some asked.
But the results were clear.

[Verse 4]
Under her management, the factory's productivity rose and accidents decreased.
From a woman's viewpoint, she also promoted a workplace where people could work more easily.
The glass ceiling — the invisible wall that blocks women's promotion — still exists today.

[Outro]
But as pioneers like Mariko increase, the wall is being broken little by little.
Gender equality is not only a women's issue.
It is also an economic necessity for maximizing the output of society as a whole.
A society cannot develop without making use of the talent of half its population.
Mariko has both the strength not to yield when confronted with obstacles and kindness toward others.
She has become a role model for the next generation of women leaders.

lessons.title: H143 — 祖母のピアノ
lessons.style: Intimate indie folk and piano ballad, 80 BPM, acoustic guitar, felt piano, cello, and very light drums. Warm, honest, and emotionally restrained, building to quiet hope rather than a huge climax. Make acoustic piano the emotional center, with the sound of memory suggested by soft room reverb. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In my old home stood an ancient piano.
It had been used by my grandmother in her youth and had the dignity of an antique.
The keys were yellowed, and the tuning was slightly off, but it was our family's treasure.

[Verse 2]
Every week my mother would gently wipe the piano, and once a year she called a tuner for its maintenance.
Music is a precious heritage of our family, she said.
From the age of six, I began lessons on this piano.

[Verse 3]
The first few years were bitter.
Practice seemed silly to me.
Hearing friends playing outside, I kept repeating scales.
But in middle school, piano gradually became enjoyable.

[Bridge]
I could play Chopin and Debussy and came to know the joy of expressing my emotions through sound.
At university I did not select music as my major.
But I continued playing the piano.

[Verse 4]
Even on busy days, the time at the keyboard was my spiritual rest.
Employment, marriage, raising children.
At every stage of life, the piano was with me.
On tired nights, sad days, joyful days.
Music absorbed my feelings and healed me.

[Outro]
My grandmother passed away, my mother passed away, and now it is my daughter who plays the piano.
My seven-year-old daughter lacks the strength in her fingertips to play Chopin.
But the sight of her stretching her toes toward the pedal recalls my own image long ago.
A single old piano has connected the family across four generations.
An instrument is not a mere object.
Like a chamber of family history and affection, it contains all the memories.

lessons.style: Intimate indie folk and piano ballad, 80 BPM, acoustic guitar, felt piano, cello, and very light drums. Warm, honest, and emotionally restrained, building to quiet hope rather than a huge climax. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
My father lost his right leg in a traffic accident when he was twenty-five.
From that time on, his life with a disability began.
The first few years were filled with despair.
Adapting to a prosthetic leg was a bitter process, and learning to walk again took months.

[Verse 2]
My father, having received such a blow, often grieved alone at night.
But my father was a strong person.
He did not yield to depression.
He accepted his disability and made up his mind to build a new life.
He began his studies at an accounting institute.

[Verse 3]
In order to qualify for a profession he could do while seated, three years later he earned the qualification of a certified public accountant.
After that, he became an independent financial consultant for small and medium-sized businesses.

[Bridge]
With precise calculations and sincere work, he won the trust of many clients.
He married my mother, and my sister and I were born.
Even with a prosthetic leg, my father played with us in the park.

[Verse 4]
He could not ride a bicycle, but he could swim with us in the pool.
My father often said, The most important thing in life is not what you have lost, but what you make from what remains.
At sixty, my father retired.

[Outro]
Today, he works as a volunteer at a local organization supporting people with disabilities.
He gives advice from his own experience to young people who have gone through the same.
To lose a part of one's body is a terrible experience.
But what my father taught me is that loss does not have to be the end of a meaningful life.
Hardship can deepen a person's understanding.
My father's quiet strength was born from the experience of losing a leg.

lessons.title: H145 — 古本屋の主人
lessons.style: Warm acoustic city-pop, 100 BPM, clean guitar, piano, melodic bass, and light live drums. Natural everyday motion, gentle nostalgia, and an unforced memorable melody. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
On a back street of the city, tucked away, there is a used bookshop.
It is not a so-called tourist spot, but it is known to lovers of books.
The owner is a gentleman in his seventies who has been selling books from this place for more than thirty years.

[Verse 2]
When you step inside, the smell of old books surrounds you.
The shelves are filled with books up to the ceiling.
Literature, history, philosophy, science.
Whatever sort of book you want, you can find it if you search.
The owner is an expert on books.

[Verse 3]
When a customer says a title, within a few minutes he remembers where on the shelf it is.
He can tell you the plot of any book.
The shop has a quiet atmosphere like a private reading room.
Customers speak in low voices and handle the books carefully.

[Bridge]
Sometimes a rare out-of-print book is brought in.
The owner promptly buys it and sells it at an appropriate price.
To deliver a book of worth to its next owner — that is his mission.
This is the age of e-books.
Sales of paper books are decreasing.

[Verse 4]
Used bookshops too are similarly shrinking in number.
But the owner is not pessimistic.
A paper book has a charm that an e-book does not, he says.
The feel in your hand, the sound of turning a page, the weight of the book itself.

[Outro]
Unlike books on a screen, you can line them on a shelf and make them part of your home.
In this shop, I have met many treasured books.
The prices are low, but the contents are superior.
The owner opens the shutter every morning, arranges the books, and waits for customers.
I will continue as long as I can continue, he says.
May this quiet place remain, at least a little longer.
That is the wish of everyone who loves books.

sections.name: Verse 3
lines: When a customer says a title, within a few minutes he remembers where on the shelf it is.
He can tell you the plot of any book.
The shop has a quiet atmosphere like a private reading room.
Customers speak in low voices and handle the books carefully.

sections.name: Bridge
lines: Sometimes a rare out-of-print book is brought in.
The owner promptly buys it and sells it at an appropriate price.
To deliver a book of worth to its next owner — that is his mission.
This is the age of e-books.
Sales of paper books are decreasing.

sections.name: Verse 4
lines: Used bookshops too are similarly shrinking in number.
But the owner is not pessimistic.
A paper book has a charm that an e-book does not, he says.
The feel in your hand, the sound of turning a page, the weight of the book itself.

sections.name: Outro
lines: Unlike books on a screen, you can line them on a shelf and make them part of your home.
In this shop, I have met many treasured books.
The prices are low, but the contents are superior.
The owner opens the shutter every morning, arranges the books, and waits for customers.
I will continue as long as I can continue, he says.
May this quiet place remain, at least a little longer.
That is the wish of everyone who loves books.

lessons.title: H146 — 田舎の夏休み
lessons.style: Intimate indie folk and piano ballad, 80 BPM, acoustic guitar, felt piano, cello, and very light drums. Warm, honest, and emotionally restrained, building to quiet hope rather than a huge climax. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
When I was a child, summer vacations were special.
Each year I would spend a month at my grandparents' house in the countryside.
My grandfather was a former farmer with a large garden and fields.

[Verse 2]
In the morning, I would go out to the field with him to harvest the vegetables.
Tomatoes, cucumbers, corn.
The vegetables that had absorbed the sunlight tasted different from what you buy in the city.
Every dinner my grandmother cooked was special.

[Verse 3]
In the afternoon, we would go swimming in the nearby creek.
The water was cold, and the stones on the bottom were rough.
When I leapt in barefoot, it was so cold I felt breathless.
In the evening, I would walk the dog with my grandfather.

[Bridge]
The Labrador, Shiro, was a wise dog who listened well to my grandfather.
At night, on the veranda, I would gaze at the starry sky with my grandmother.
Countless stars that could not be seen in the city would blink at me.

[Verse 4]
My grandmother would quietly tell me the stories of the constellations.
After I moved to the city for university, my chances to visit the countryside grew fewer.
After my grandparents passed away, the house passed into other hands.

[Outro]
But when summer comes, I still remember those countryside summers.
Now as an adult, I take my own children to the countryside where my wife's parents live.
There are fields, a creek, and at night a sky full of stars.
Seeing my children chase insects with sparkling eyes and try to catch fish in the river, I feel my younger self is being restored.
A country summer passed down across generations.
There is something in it that the convenience of the city cannot replace.

lessons.title: H147 — 貧困のサイクル
lessons.style: Solemn cinematic chamber ballad, 74 BPM, low strings, sparse piano, distant ambient texture, and restrained percussion. Compassionate and anti-sensational, with no triumphant or militaristic feeling. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In this world, there are invisible borders of many kinds.
Some are clear, like national borders.
Others are invisible walls within society.
One of these is the cycle of poverty.

[Verse 2]
A child born into a poor family has limited educational opportunities, cannot get a good job, and, even as an adult, cannot escape from poverty.
This is passed on from one generation to the next generation.
To break this cycle requires the effort of society as a whole.

[Verse 3]
Education, medical care, housing, job training.
Through one individual's strength alone, it is difficult to escape poverty.
Bangladesh's Grameen Bank created a new scheme against poverty.
Microfinance — small loans to low-income people.
Money is lent, even without collateral.
The repayment rate is surprisingly high.

[Bridge]
It demonstrated that poor people are not lazy.
Given only the chance, they succeed through their own power.
The founder Muhammad Yunus received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2006.
Yunus argued that poverty reflects social systems rather than personal failure.
Meanwhile, in developed countries too, a new poverty has emerged.

[Verse 4]
The working poor, who can only make ends meet despite long hours.
A divide in education caused by parents' income.
Poverty not only torments those who experience it, but also blocks the development of society as a whole.

[Outro]
A society in which every person can make use of their talent is a sustainable society.
This is not a distant story.
Beside us, even now, someone is fighting against poverty.
What we can do — for each one of us to think about it — is the first step.

lessons.title: H148 — 警察と社会
lessons.style: Thoughtful cinematic indie pop, 88 BPM, steady 4/4, warm piano, brushed drums, subtle bass pulse, and restrained low strings. Dignified documentary mood that gradually opens toward hope. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
A police officer, that is, a cop, is an important profession that protects the order of society.
They patrol the streets around the clock and react to incidents and accidents.
Their work involves many areas.

[Verse 2]
Investigating a crime, enforcing traffic laws, consulting with residents, responding to reports of suspicious activity while respecting civil rights.
There are dramatic scenes of tracking down a killer, but much of daily duty is steady, quiet work.
Writing documents, investigating the scene, communication with a supervisor.

[Verse 3]
The role of correctional facilities that manage prisoners is also important.
The aim is not only to punish criminals but also to rehabilitate them.
But the work of police has dangerous moments.
Armed criminals, gunshots, explosions.
They often face risks to their own lives.

[Bridge]
Police function only with the trust of citizens.
If there is violence or corruption, their reputation is lost in an instant.
In America, excessive violence against Black people has continued, and the Black Lives Matter movement has spread.

[Verse 4]
This is not a rebellion against the entire police but a voice demanding reform.
Japanese police are called affectionately Omawari-san.
The koban (police box) system is unique in the world, providing local community-based security.
Police officers too are human.
They make mistakes, and they have emotions.

[Outro]
While we expect much of them, we must not demand perfection.
Mutual understanding and cooperation are the foundation of a safe society.

lessons.title: H149 — 倉庫で働くということ
lessons.style: Clean modern rhythmic indie pop, 96 BPM, muted electric piano, soft plucked synth, precise bass, and light electronic-acoustic drums. Intelligent, energetic, and easy to follow without sounding corporate. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Warehouse work is unglamorous but essential to society.
The storage of goods, sorting, and delivery.
Without these, modern distribution does not work.
Having dropped out of high school, I began working at a large Amazon warehouse at twenty-two.
At first it was simple manual labor, but gradually I learned the work.

[Verse 2]
Warehouse work has technical aspects too.
Working alongside robots.
Barcode scanners, picking systems, conveyors.
I learned these material handling technologies.
From seven in the morning until six in the evening, I walked around until my feet seemed to sink.
Sometimes my knees hurt.

[Verse 3]
At lunchtime I would eat my bento box on my lap and read messages from my partner.
But I was proud of this work.
Whatever goods we delivered, someone was waiting.
Someone's birthday gift, someone's urgent tool for work.
After five years of work, I got a promotion to team leader.

[Bridge]
I was responsible for analyzing my team's work logs and proposed improvements for efficiency.
But the warehouse industry is now in the middle of great change.
Automation, AI, robots.
Simple labor is disappearing.
My intention is to continue studying at night school to keep up with this change.

[Verse 4]
I am not a university graduate, but the experience I have gained on the floor is valuable.
I want to build a society where people are not judged by academic background alone.
A society in which whoever works sincerely is properly rewarded.

[Outro]
On my resume, my warehouse experience is written with pride.
It was my starting point and the work that has supported my life.

lessons.title: H150 — 2050年の食卓
lessons.style: Forward-looking cinematic synth-pop, 100 BPM, warm arpeggiated synth, piano, rounded electronic bass, and clean hybrid drums. Curious and human rather than robotic, with controlled futuristic color. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
By 2050, the world is predicted to have a population of 9.7 billion.
How to feed such a rapidly growing population is one of the greatest challenges in human history.
Food production is said to need to increase by 70 percent from today.
But we cannot increase arable land.

[Verse 2]
Rather, through climate change and desertification, the land suitable for farming is shrinking.
A shift to plant-based foods rich in fiber, reducing excessive meat consumption, and eating insects.
These alternatives are being proposed.
Vertical farming is gaining attention.
Inside buildings in cities, vegetables are grown hydroponically.

[Verse 3]
Without needing extensive farmland, fresh vegetables can be supplied from the urban outskirts.
Gene-editing technology also offers hope.
Crops that increase yields, resist pests, and endure flood and drought.
It is an issue that brings both promise and concern.
The problem of meat is also serious.

[Bridge]
The livestock industry emits huge amounts of greenhouse gases.
Cultured meat — meat grown in a factory — may be an alternative that reduces environmental burdens.
The problem of food waste cannot be overlooked.
One-third of food produced in the world is thrown away.
Just reducing this alone could feed many people.

[Verse 4]
There is something we can do at the individual level too.
Plan meals, use leftovers, and reduce food waste.
Choose locally produced ingredients.
Gradually reduce meat consumption.
Food is the basis of survival and the core of culture.

[Outro]
The future dining table is built by the sum of choices made by each of us.
Our love for the Earth should be reflected in our food choices too.

lessons.title: H151 — 核兵器と日本
lessons.style: Solemn cinematic chamber ballad, 74 BPM, low strings, sparse piano, distant ambient texture, and restrained percussion. Compassionate and anti-sensational, with no triumphant or militaristic feeling. Use a memorial tone; no explosion effects, military drums, or triumphant climax. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Abolition of nuclear weapons may sound idealistic.
But in Japan, which experienced Hiroshima and Nagasaki, this is necessarily an unavoidable theme.
Today, there are about 12,500 nuclear warheads in the world.
Most are held by the United States and Russia.

[Verse 2]
Their military value is said to lie in being unusable weapons that exercise deterrence.
But deterrence may, like a flood, sweep everything away.
A wrong judgment, an accident, a seizure by terrorists.
Once used, the civilized world ends.

[Verse 3]
Survivors of the bombs have kept telling their partly remembered stories.
Burnt skin, radiation sickness, black rain.
Things a human must not do to another human.
In 2017, the Treaty on the Prohibition of Nuclear Weapons was adopted at the UN.

[Bridge]
122 countries voted in favor, but all nuclear-armed states were excluded.
Japan, though the only country to have been bombed, did not join the treaty because of its security policy.
This contradiction is a great issue in Japanese society.

[Verse 4]
Depending on America's nuclear umbrella while calling for abolition.
This tension remains the subject of ethical and security debate.
Nuclear weapons, once made, are hard to remove.
But humanity has banned chemical and biological weapons too.

[Outro]

Today, there are about 12,500 nuclear warheads in the world.
Most are held by the United States and Russia.
Their military value is said to lie in being unusable weapons that exercise deterrence.
But deterrence may, like a flood, sweep everything away.
A wrong judgment, an accident, a seizure by terrorists.
Once used, the civilized world ends.
Survivors of the bombs have kept telling their partly remembered stories.
Burnt skin, radiation sickness, black rain.

This tension remains the subject of ethical and security debate.

lessons.style: Warm world-folk art-pop, 92 BPM, acoustic strings, piano, hand percussion, and carefully restrained regional color. Respectful, contemporary, and never novelty music or caricature. Add a respectful modal clarinet and cello color, avoiding stereotyped or celebratory caricature. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The Jewish religion has a history of 3,500 years.
It is also a root of Christianity and Islam.
The stories of the Old Testament are among the most widely read of humanity's myths.

[Verse 2]
Noah's Ark, Moses leading the Exodus, David and Goliath.
These stories form the principal foundation of Western culture.
The history of the Jewish people has also been a history of persecution.
Exile by ancient Rome, discrimination in medieval Europe, the twentieth-century Holocaust.

[Verse 3]
Extensive discrimination continued.
Yet Jewish communities continued to preserve their own culture and faith.
Worship at the synagogue, the Sabbath, the Passover.
Tradition was passed down across generations.
Jewish culture, which values knowledge, produced many outstanding figures.
Einstein, Freud, Kafka, Spielberg.

[Bridge]
Scholarship, art, business, science.
In every field, Jewish contributions should be credited.
But today's Israeli-Palestinian conflict is a serious problem.
Since the founding of Israel in 1948, the conflict between the two has continued.

[Verse 4]
Both sides have justified claims, and both have victims.
Religion and ethnicity hold the power to generate both love and hatred.
Rather than exclude others, to choose coexistence.
That is the goal of a civilized society.

[Outro]
Religion can be a tool that divides people, or a tool that unites them.
That choice lies in the hands of each believer.

lessons.title: H153 — 金箔職人の40年
lessons.style: Warm world-folk art-pop, 92 BPM, acoustic strings, piano, hand percussion, and carefully restrained regional color. Respectful, contemporary, and never novelty music or caricature. Blend restrained Japanese plucked-string color with modern piano, emphasizing craft and patience. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In the world of Japanese traditional crafts, there are techniques that have continued for hundreds of years.
Kyoto lacquerware, Ishikawa's Wajima lacquer, Okinawa's Ryukyu glass.
Artisans often begin with a long apprenticeship.
Mr. Tanaka, a gold leaf artisan in Kanazawa, has walked this path for forty years.

[Verse 2]
The work of making gold leaf of 0.0001 millimeters thick is largely done by hand.
He beats gold and extends it thin.
Without skilled technique, the gold tears.
Mr. Tanaka's hands are proof of forty years of doing this work.
Gold leaf is used on Buddhist statues, temples, and crafts.

[Verse 3]
It is an essential material for the expression of Japanese art.
But the successor problem is serious.
Young people go to cities and choose industrialized, mass-production work.
Few young people learn the handmade craft.
Mr. Tanaka too keeps searching for apprentices.

[Bridge]
But the belief that it does not make money keeps the young at a distance.
The government also increases investment to protect traditional crafts.
A system for passing down skills, grants for young artisans, expanding sales abroad.
The power of social media is also great.

[Verse 4]
Mr. Tanaka posts the process of making gold leaf on Instagram.
Interest from people overseas has begun to influence young Japanese too.
Tradition is not something to be preserved, but something to be kept alive.
Adapting to the modern era in new forms while not losing the core technique.

[Outro]
That is true succession.
Mr. Tanaka says, Whether this skill will remain a hundred years from now depends on the choice of each one of us.

lessons.title: H154 — 定年退職とクルーズ
lessons.style: Sunlit acoustic pop with subtle bossa and world-folk hints, 102 BPM, nylon guitar, soft hand percussion, piano, and warm bass. Open, observant, and gently cinematic. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Having worked for thirty years as the deputy branch manager of a bank, I retired at the mandatory age.
On my last day, my younger colleagues gave me a bouquet and a handwritten letter.
The letter said, Thank you for the things you reminded us of.

[Verse 2]
I had never been an imposing manager, but I had urged sincerity in my subordinates.
After retirement, my wife and I set off on an around-the-world trip on a luxury cruise ship.
Three months at sea.
The ship traveled the Mediterranean, the African coast, and the Gulf of Mexico.

[Verse 3]
At each port we bought items.
But even luxurious days grow tiring.
Lavish meals, dinners in formal dress, and polished evening music.
A pretty similar pattern continued every day.
My wife and I, moreover, gained more time to talk.

[Bridge]
It was time to rebuild the close relationship we had not been able to have in our working years.
Our son's birthday, our daughter's wedding, the story of how we helped raise our grandchildren.
We would record our memories while also talking about plans for the future.

[Verse 4]
The guests on the ship, as an observer would see, were diverse.
Retired bankers, writers, lawyers.
Everyone had walked a different life.
We talked with an elderly couple.
The husband was seventy-six.
Life is a continuing series of stages, he laughed.
Life has stages.
Youth, maturity, old age.

[Outro]
Each stage has its own unique beauty.
I want to live the rest of my life with gratitude.

lessons.title: H155 — 戦場から帰った兵士
lessons.style: Solemn cinematic chamber ballad, 74 BPM, low strings, sparse piano, distant ambient texture, and restrained percussion. Compassionate and anti-sensational, with no triumphant or militaristic feeling. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Soldiers who come back from a battle site may find that the battle does not end when they return to society.
Substance abuse, suicide, family collapse due to PTSD.
Even if one survives the war, lives can still be lost in the years that follow.

[Verse 2]
My friend Michael was a US soldier who fought in Iraq.
After returning home, he would panic or become angry even at small sounds.
The sound of fireworks, the slam of a car door.
These reminded him of the explosions of the battlefield.

[Verse 3]
Michael also could not sleep and suffered from nightmares.
His wife tried to support him.
But life with him, as he grew aggressive, was hard.
Michael then came to rely on drugs.
A veterans' support organization reached out to him.
Counseling, group therapy, dialogue with comrades.

[Bridge]
Michael slowly recovered.
Now he does work to support other veterans.
War may break you.
But it does not have to define you.
Politicians start wars, but it is the young who fight.

[Verse 4]
Care after return is the responsibility of the nation that sent them to war.
It is not only soldiers who suffer PTSD.
Victims of abuse, those struck by disaster.
Because wounds of the heart are invisible, they remain long.

[Outro]
For society to turn its eyes to the wounds of the heart and build a system of support.
That is the condition of a kind society.

lessons.title: H156 — LGBTQ+の権利
lessons.style: Thoughtful cinematic indie pop, 88 BPM, steady 4/4, warm piano, brushed drums, subtle bass pulse, and restrained low strings. Dignified documentary mood that gradually opens toward hope. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In 2022, debate over LGBTQ+ rights grew active.
Marriage for gay couples, respect for gender identity, the enactment of a non-discrimination law.
Japan has traditionally been said to have little plain prejudice against sexual minorities.
But institutional support has lagged.
To assure same-sex marriage requires legal reform.

[Verse 2]
But in the Diet, the proposal has repeatedly been abandoned.
Tokyo and many other local governments have introduced same-sex partnership systems.
Overseas, the situation is different.
Countries recognizing same-sex marriage now include many countries and jurisdictions.
The United States, Canada, France, Germany, the Netherlands, Taiwan.

[Verse 3]
Opponents emphasize on traditional family values.
But what is tradition?
Is something correct simply because it has continued from the past?
Younger generations are possibly more open on this issue.
Some polls show over 80 percent of university students support same-sex marriage.
Companies are moving too.

[Bridge]
Workplace environments that respect LGBTQ+ people.
Diversity is a source of competitive strength.
There are additional issues for transgender people.
Strict requirements apply to changing legal gender.
There is diversity in how people live their sexuality.

[Outro]
The right for each person to live as themselves is one of the basic human rights.

lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
In Japanese communities, old legends remain.
Fox, tanuki, kappa, tengu.
Demons of hell.
Stories about them have been passed down since childhood.
These youkai are not mere products of imagination.
They embodied the wisdom of our ancestors, used to explain natural phenomena.

[Verse 2]
The fox is said to be the messenger of the deity Inari.
Like a servant of the shrine, fox statues guard the entrance.
The kappa is said to live near rivers.
It has a dish on its head filled with water.

[Verse 3]
Adults would urge children, Be careful at rivers.
The tengu lives in mountainous regions and has a red face and a long nose.
It would test mountain ascetics.
These stories taught children awe and fear of nature.

[Bridge]
They emphasized that humans cannot rule nature.

As traditional customs are being lost through urbanization, youkai continue to live in new forms.

They are a source for the imagination of creators.
Even in the age of rationalism, when everything seems explainable, we have not lost our sense of the invisible.
At night, walking a mountain path, one suddenly turns and feels something is there.

[Outro]
That sense is the core of Japanese youkai culture.

lessons.title: H158 — 海外で暮らして
lessons.style: Sunlit acoustic pop with subtle bossa and world-folk hints, 102 BPM, nylon guitar, soft hand percussion, piano, and warm bass. Open, observant, and gently cinematic. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Living abroad, one sees both the good and the bad of one's own country.
At thirty, I was posted to the United States for three years for work.
The first months brought surprise from cultural differences.
Ordering for yourself at restaurants, the gesture of a shrug.

[Verse 2]
Different kept appearing.
Americans are direct.
They do not try to hide their opinions or emotions.
If they disagree, they argue clearly, openly.
On the other hand, there is casualness.
With someone in the same elevator, small talk that is not rude begins immediately.

[Verse 3]
But I also saw the dark side.
Gun crime, racial discrimination, the high cost of medical care.
Millions of people have no health insurance, and if they get sick, they must fall deeply into debt.

[Bridge]
A homeless person carrying their gear lies at the foot of a skyscraper.
Returning to Japan, I realized anew: safety, cleanliness, the precision of time.
In Japan, you can see a person walking alone at a station late at night.
You would not see this in America.

[Verse 4]
But Japan has its weaknesses too.
Conformity pressure, overwork, high suicide rates.
The individual is weak, and people, often pay too much attention to the eyes of others.
The experience of another culture is a mirror.

[Outro]
While you come to know the other country, you see your own country more clearly.
Experience abroad is made up of individual encounters.
Together, they have shaped me as a person.

lessons.title: H159 — 医学研究所の発表
lessons.style: Atmospheric cinematic synth-pop, 84 BPM, glassy pads, soft mallets, delicate arpeggiators, piano, and slowly widening strings. A sense of discovery, scale, and quiet wonder. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
The National Institute of Medicine in Tokyo is a cutting-edge lab.
The director is Dr.
Tanaka, the deputy is Dr.
Sato.
Today's event is the final presentation of a joint research project.

[Verse 2]
Through collaboration with an American university, a new drug has been developed.
The secretary, Yamada-san, prepared the presentation.
The participants are male and female, in roughly equal numbers.
In the presentation, Dr.
Tanaka explained the properties of the new drug's liquid compound.

[Verse 3]
Even a tiny unit for experiments has an effect, with few side effects.
The new drug was developed for cancer patients facing an urgent need for new treatment.
The conditions of the clinical trial were strict, conducted over two years.

[Bridge]
The participants' data were arranged in string-like graphs and projected on slides.
The researchers stare at the screen.
For transport of the drug load, steel containers are used.
Temperature control is important.

[Verse 4]
The graduate students of the lab also contributed to this achievement.
Maybe in a few years, they will be the next leaders.
Dr. Tanaka, with a wan smile, said, This drug will save many lives.

[Outro]
I want to thank the research team who deserve the credit.
After the meeting, the participants headed towards the hotel for the dinner gathering.
Science advances through the power of teamwork.

lessons.title: H160 — パリのファッション週間
lessons.style: Sophisticated cinematic art-pop, 92 BPM, expressive piano, elegant strings, clean bass, and lightly asymmetric percussion. Visually evocative, emotionally mature, and rhythmically clear. Add chic Parisian art-pop and subtle chanson color, with crisp runway momentum and no cabaret parody. Clear young-adult English lead vocal with neutral pronunciation and precise consonants. Mature high-school educational tone, memorable but not childish. Verse-led through-composed arrangement; sing every lyric line exactly once, with no repeated chorus. Restrained melodic range, short instrumental intro, very light outro. No rap, no spoken narration, no ad-libs, no choir-heavy ending, no excessive melisma, no Japanese lyrics.
lessons.lyrics_block:
[Verse 1]
Fashion week, Paris.
The world's top designers present their new collections.
The models walking the runway look like beautiful paintings.
They wear high-heeled shoes and gorgeous dresses.
A crown of flowers decorates their heads, as if they were queens.

[Verse 2]
Backstage, staff run about in a hurry.
We have no time, someone mutters.
Makeup corrections, hair adjustments, final checks on costumes.
The smell of staff meals drifts from the pan.
After long hours of work, both staff and models are hungry.

[Verse 3]
The designer apologizes, I am sorry we have asked you to work without a proper break.
But once the show begins, everything is beautiful like magic.
With each step the models take, the venue holds its breath.
Fashion is not mere clothing.

[Bridge]
It is a means of self-expression and a statement to society.
In recent years, the fashion industry has been forced to change greatly.
Environmental issues, workers' rights, diversity.
Criticism of fast fashion is rising.
Young designers advocate ethical fashion.

[Verse 4]
Use of recycled materials, fair labor conditions, inclusion of diverse body types.
Clothes should be made in a way that does not sacrifice the Earth.
Major brands too are slowly changing.

[Outro]
The pressure of if we do not change, we will not survive moves the whole industry.
Fashion is a mirror of its era.
The clothes we choose reveal what we value.
